title: [inkx] scrollTo in LAYOUT_PROPS causes unnecessary layout recalculation
description:
## Summary
scrollTo is in LAYOUT_PROPS (helpers.ts:50), so every scroll change triggers a full layout recalculation via layoutNode.markDirty().

## Evidence
- Before scroll: layout phase takes 10-50ms
- After scrolling right past edge: layout phase jumps to 150-400ms
- Scrolling back left: returns to 10-15ms

## Root Cause
Right columns likely have more nodes. When scrollTo changes, the entire tree is marked dirty and flexx recalculates layout for ALL nodes - not just visible ones.

## Fix
Remove scrollTo from LAYOUT_PROPS in `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/reconciler/helpers.ts`.

scrollTo doesn't affect layout dimensions - it only determines scroll offset in scrollPhase, which runs on every render anyway and reads props.scrollTo directly. The layout engine (flexx/yoga) never sees scrollTo.

## Alternative
Add a separate scrollPropsChanged check that marks a different flag (e.g., scrollDirty) that only triggers scroll recalculation, not full layout.

## Source
Reported by another agent investigating slow scrolling in inkx.
close_reason: Removed scrollTo from LAYOUT_PROPS in helpers.ts. scrollTo doesn't affect layout dimensions - only scroll offset handled in scrollPhase.

title: inkx VirtualList: scrollToIndex calculation produces wrong child index
description:
## Problem
The scrollToIndex calculation can become negative when clampedIndex < startIndex:

const selectedIndexInSlice = clampedIndex - startIndex;
const scrollToIndex = hasTopPlaceholder ? selectedIndexInSlice + 1 : selectedIndexInSlice;

If selectedIndexInSlice is negative, Math.max(0, scrollToIndex) clamps it to 0, scrolling to the top placeholder instead of the intended item.

## Location
vendor/beorn-inkx/src/components/VirtualList.tsx lines 233-246

When childHeight > viewportHeight, the inner Math.min produces a negative number that gets clamped to 0.

description: When switching between storybook sections in interactive mode, stray characters from the previous render appear at the right edge of content lines. Root cause: inkx doesn't clear to end-of-line when new content is narrower than previous frame. Visible in bun storybook interactive mode when navigating between sections of different widths.
notes:
Actual fix (2026-02-05): Two root causes found and fixed in inkx reconciler:

1. **Layout-phase subtreeDirty propagation**: When a node's layout position changes, ancestors were not marked subtreeDirty, causing content-phase to fast-path skip unchanged subtrees that actually needed re-rendering. Fixed in layout-phase.ts. (61→12 INKX_STRICT errors)

2. **Virtual text dirty flag propagation**: appendChild/removeChild/insertBefore/commitUpdate on virtual text nodes (nested <Text> without layoutNode) called layoutNode?.markDirty() which was a no-op. Added markLayoutAncestorDirty() helper that walks up to the nearest layout ancestor and sets contentDirty+paintDirty+layoutDirty+markDirty(). (12→0 INKX_STRICT errors)

Commit: 5a4cc45 in inkx, 8349d4e4 in km
close_reason: Diagnostic tests confirm buffer and ANSI replay are correct. Added comprehensive withDiagnostics test suite (diag-ghost-chars.test.tsx) covering board driver and storybook patterns. Exported outputPhase from inkx/toolbelt. Updated skills with rendering bug workflow. If ghost chars reappear, the diagnostic tooling needs enhancement to cover the specific pattern (e.g., real terminal timing, cursor visibility).

title: Incremental rendering skips absolute-positioned elements when siblings change
description:
When board content changes (e.g., typing in search dialog), absolute-positioned dialog elements with unchanged React content don't get repainted. All dirty flags are false on the dialog's title node, so the incremental fast-path skips it entirely.

INKX_STRICT=1 confirms: IncrementalRenderMismatchError at the dialog title position — incremental shows space, fresh shows the correct character.

Root cause: renderer.ts incremental rendering doesn't propagate dirty flags to absolute-positioned siblings when content changes in the normal flow.

Workaround: testEnv now uses incremental: false. Production still has this bug (visible when typing in search dialog — title flickers).

Blocker for enabling INKX_STRICT=1 globally in tests.
close_reason: Fixed with two-pass absolute child rendering in content-phase.ts. Normal-flow children render first, then absolute children on top (CSS paint order). This ensures clearNodeRegion from dirty siblings never overwrites absolute child pixels. Committed in inkx ebe351e.

title: inkx: Background color bleeds across wrapped text lines
description:
## Problem
When Text with backgroundColor wraps to multiple lines, the background color bleeds
across all wrapped lines instead of being constrained to each line's content bounds.

## Root Cause
The issue is in inkx's `collectTextContent` function (render-text.ts). When processing
nested Text elements, it embeds backgroundColor as ANSI codes in the collected text string
via `applyTextStyleAnsi`. 

When this text is then wrapped by `wrapAnsi`, the ANSI codes are preserved within the
text content. Since we reset+restore parent styles after each child element, the background
persists across line breaks.

## Reproduction
See km storybook View 1 (Cards) - the selected card "Implement auth flow" has yellow
background that extends to the second line "flow" and beyond.

## Potential Fix
The proper fix would be to NOT embed backgroundColor as ANSI codes in `collectTextContent`.
Instead, background should be handled at the buffer level similar to how Box backgroundColor
works - fill the layout bounds first, then render text on top.

This requires architectural changes to how nested Text styling works in inkx.

## Files
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/pipeline/render-text.ts - collectTextContent, applyTextStyleAnsi
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/pipeline/render-box.ts - shows how Box bg works (buffer fill)
close_reason: Fixed: moved Text backgroundColor from ANSI embedding to buffer-level application. collectTextWithBg() tracks bg color as BgSegment character ranges, maps them through wrapping, and applies to buffer cells directly.

title: Border-box model: text bleeds into right border of Box with borderStyle
description:
inkx uses content-box model for bordered boxes — text is rendered as if the full width is available, causing it to bleed into the right border character. This forces consumers to manually subtract border width (width-2, paddingRight={1}, etc.) as workarounds.

The fix: inkx should implement border-box sizing where the usable content width automatically excludes border characters. A Box with width=40 and borderStyle='single' should have 38 chars of content width, not 40.

Related: km-tui.card-border-bleed (closed with workaround, real fix deferred to inkx). Currently worked around with paddingRight={1} in CardColumn.tsx — should be removed once this is fixed.
notes:
Confirmed visible in FAMILY SCHEDULE column header — last char 'E' eaten by right border. Also affects column header text width calculations generally.
Session 0219f investigation: NOT an inkx bug. 14 tests prove border-box model correct (flexx + yoga). Real cause was km-tui column width-1 handling (already fixed in km-tui.card-border-bleed). Recommend closing.
close_reason: Not an inkx bug. Border-box model correct (14 new tests confirm). Was a km-tui width calculation issue, already fixed in prior session.

title: Text content bleeds into right border of Box with borderStyle

This bug has been reported and worked around 3+ times — each time the workaround gets removed, text bleeds into borders. The fix belongs in inkx's layout pipeline.

Added regression test in vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/border-text-overflow.test.tsx (4 tests). Updated card-layout and cursor-border-overflow test assertions.

title: Discuss replacing custom selector with css-select
description:
## Context

inkx currently has a custom CSS selector implementation (~150 lines) in vendor/beorn-inkx/src/testing/locator.ts that supports:
- ID selectors: #id
- Attribute selectors: [attr], [attr="value"], [attr^="prefix"], etc.
- Compound selectors: #id[attr="value"]
- Combinators: descendant (space), child (>), adjacent sibling (+)

## Alternative: css-select

css-select is a popular library (45M weekly downloads, 592 GitHub stars) that provides full CSS3/4 selector support.

**Pros:**
- Comprehensive: supports pseudo-classes (:nth-child, :not(), :has(), etc.)
- Battle-tested: used by cheerio, htmlparser2, and many others
- Well-maintained: active development, good documentation

**Cons:**
- Requires custom adapter (~12 functions: getChildren, getParent, getName, getAttributeValue, etc.)
- External dependency (adds to bundle size)
- Overkill for current test needs (tests only use basic selectors)

## Trade-offs

**Code size comparison:**
- Custom implementation: ~150 lines total
- css-select approach: ~50-100 lines adapter + library dependency

**When to consider switching:**
- If tests need pseudo-classes or advanced selectors
- If maintenance burden of custom code becomes high
- If multiple projects need the same selector engine

## Recommendation

**Keep custom implementation for now** unless:
1. Tests start requiring advanced selectors
2. Bugs in custom implementation become frequent
3. Community requests pseudo-class support

## Resources

- css-select npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/css-select
- css-select GitHub: https://github.com/fb55/css-select
- Custom implementation: vendor/beorn-inkx/src/testing/locator.ts
close_reason: Decision made: keep custom implementation per recommendation. Custom selector is ~150 lines, covers all test needs. No pseudo-class requirements or bugs have emerged.

title: cursorMoveDown/Up stuck at wrap boundaries when stickyX=0
description: At word-wrap boundaries, cursorMoveDown/cursorMoveUp return the same offset as the current cursor position, causing the cursor to get stuck. Root cause: cursorToRowCol assigns wrap-boundary offsets to the end of line N. cursorMoveDown targets startOffset of line N+1, which equals the end of line N. With stickyX=0, the computed position equals the current position. Fix: loop through successive lines until a different position is found.
close_reason: Fix: Loop through successive lines in cursorMoveDown/cursorMoveUp to skip wrap-boundary positions where the target offset equals the current cursor. Test: 2 regression tests in text-cursor.test.ts (walk-down and walk-up with stickyX=0 on word-wrapped text). Verified: 2083 inkx tests + 1502 km-tui tests pass.

title: Blank screen when debug logging triggers Console layout cascade in incremental renderer
description: When running with DEBUG_LOG=/tmp/debug.log DEBUG='-flexx:layout,*' km view /tmp/vt, the screen goes completely blank after initial render. Only card borders update on cursor move. Root cause: debug output → console.debug() → patchConsole → Console component state update → Console text grows → layout phase runs → flexGrow sibling (board content) shrinks → content phase: board container layoutChanged=true → parentRegionCleared=true → clears entire board region → children should re-render but something in the cascade produces blank cells. INKX_STRICT confirms mismatch at (0,0) render #2: incremental fg=null bg=null vs fresh fg=8 bg=7. The dimColor fix (Bug #1) resolved the non-debug case. This bug only manifests when debug logging is active because Console component grows, triggering layout cascade.
close_reason: Root cause: ancestorCleared propagated through nodes with backgroundColor, causing Text children to clear parent's opaque bg fill. Fix: backgroundColor acts as barrier for ancestorCleared propagation (content-phase.ts:705). 3 regression tests added.

title: perf(inkx): diff micro-optimizations (bounding box, relative cursor, row slice compare)
description:
Three micro-optimizations for the output phase diff path:

1. **Dirty row bounding box**: Track minDirtyRow/maxDirtyRow during content phase so diffBuffers() loops [min,max] instead of [0,height). Saves dirty-flag checks for clean regions above/below.

2. **Relative cursor moves**: Use ESC[C/ESC[B for small cursor jumps (1-3 cells) instead of absolute ESC[y;xH (saves 2-5 bytes per move).

3. **Row-level metadata slice compare**: Before per-cell cellEquals(), compare the row's packed Uint32Array metadata as a slice. If all 32-bit values match, only need to check chars array. Avoids per-cell function call overhead for unchanged rows that are marked dirty (e.g., due to fill()).
close_reason: Implemented 3 micro-optimizations: dirty row bounding box (4.4x faster no-change output), row-level bulk compare, relative cursor moves. All tests pass.

title: DOM-like render API with nested mounting
description:
Improve inkx render API ergonomics with a DOM-like model:

## Current API (verbose)
```typescript
using term = createTerm()
const { waitUntilExit } = await render(term, <InlineProgress />, {
  mode: "inline",
  exitOnCtrlC: true,
})
await waitUntilExit()
```

## Proposed API
```typescript
// render() accepts AutoLocator as mount target
const layout = await render(term, <Layout />)
const header = await render(layout.locator('#header'), <StatusBar />)
const content = await render(layout.locator('#content'), <Board />)

// Parallel mounting
await Promise.all([
  render(layout.locator('#header'), <StatusBar />),
  render(layout.locator('#content'), <Board />),
])
```

## Key concepts
- `term.root` represents the terminal as a DOM root
- `App.locator()` returns AutoLocator which can be a render target
- Multiple React trees can mount into different regions
- Aligns with existing inkx patterns (AutoLocator, App interface)

## Implementation notes
- Extend render() to accept AutoLocator as first arg
- AutoLocator.boundingBox() provides the mount region
- Each render creates independent React reconciler root
- Parent layouts reserve space, children fill it

Reference: React 18's createRoot(container).render(<App />) pattern

title: Move text truncation from ANSI-level to layout-level
description:
Move text truncation (wrap='truncate') from ANSI-level post-processing to DOM-level in inkx's render pipeline. Currently truncation happens by parsing ANSI strings (constrainText/sliceAnsi in inkx unicode.ts). This is fragile — every new escape type (OSC 8, etc.) is a new bug surface.

The fix: truncate text content at the DOM node level before ANSI serialization. The renderer only outputs what the layout says is visible. This makes OSC 8, hyperlinks, and other escape sequences safe by construction — they're never generated for content that won't be displayed.

Keep constrainText/sliceAnsi as general-purpose ANSI utility functions (useful for non-DOM contexts), but the renderer shouldn't rely on them for layout truncation.

This subsumes km-tui.osc8-card-body — once truncation is DOM-level, OSC 8 sequences are never generated for truncated content.
close_reason: Added DOM-level text truncation via maxDisplayWidth budget in collectTextWithBg. Text is truncated at the DOM node level BEFORE ANSI serialization, making OSC 8 hyperlinks safe by construction. Uses getTextWidth (ANSI-aware) for budget tracking and sliceByWidth for trimming leaf text. Only applies to truncate-end modes. Fixes: plainLen field in TextWithBg tracks display width for correct BgSegment offset accounting. Tests: text-truncate-width.test.tsx (5 tests), board-features.spec.ts truncation test, ink-compat truncate-start/middle tests all pass.

title: Board freezes on cursor nav with detail pane open (doRender clone resets dirty rows)
description:
Board visually freezes when navigating with j/k while detail pane is open. Breadcrumb, card borders, and detail pane content all fail to update.

Root cause: TerminalBuffer.clone() resets all dirty rows to 0. When multiple doRender() calls occur per event batch (from store subscriptions), doRender #2+ clones the buffer from #1 (dirty rows reset), finds no node dirty flags (cleared by #1), writes no cells, so dirty rows stay at 0. runtime.render() then diffs against this clean buffer and diffBuffers() finds no dirty rows, producing patchLen=0.

Fix: Early return in doRender() — after React reconciliation, if root has no dirty flags and we already have a buffer, skip the pipeline entirely. Avoids creating a new clone that resets dirty rows, and naturally reduces excessive doRender calls from ~7 to ~1 per keystroke.

File: vendor/beorn-inkx/src/runtime/create-app.tsx (lines 764-777)
Verified: TTY testing confirms j/k/l navigation with detail pane updates correctly.
close_reason: Fixed: early return in doRender() skips pipeline when no dirty flags, avoiding TerminalBuffer.clone() dirty row reset. Verified via TTY.

title: inkx: Input Layer Stack for dialog input handling
description:
DOM-style input layer stack with event bubbling for dialog input handling.

## Problem
- `/china` search hangs and input is eaten
- Race condition: dialog's useInput registers async via useEffect
- Heavy query blocks everything while input handlers aren't ready

## Solution
Input layer stack with DOM-style bubbling:
```
InputBox layer   → handles text editing (chars, backspace, ctrl+shortcuts)
   ↓ bubbles if not handled (returns false)
dialog layer     → handles dialog-specific keys (enter=confirm, escape=cancel)
   ↓ bubbles if not handled
board layer      → handles navigation commands
   ↓ bubbles if not handled
app layer        → handles global (quit, help)
```

InputBox becomes a focusable element that can receive input, similar to DOM focus.

## Implementation
1. InputLayerContext + InputLayerProvider in inkx
2. useInputLayer hook (sync registration via useLayoutEffect)
3. Integrate with withKeybindings (single useInput dispatches to stack)
4. Make InputBox a layer that handles text editing

## Files
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/contexts/InputLayerContext.tsx (new)
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/hooks/useInputLayer.ts (new)
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/index.ts

See docs/future/inkx-command-api-research.md

title: inkx: incremental contentPhase rendering
description:
## Problem

contentPhase processes ALL nodes every frame (~31µs/node), even when React only updated 2 components. This causes O(n) render time where n=total nodes, not changed nodes.

With 6668 nodes, contentPhase takes 210ms even though only 2 TreeCards changed.

## Root Cause

React's reconciler knows exactly which components changed, but inkx ignores this:
- React marks 2 nodes as needing update
- inkx walks all 6668 nodes anyway
- Each node is written to TerminalBuffer regardless of change

## Research Context (Deep Research, Feb 2026)

Modern TUI frameworks solve this:
- **Ratatui**: "compares the current buffer to the new buffer each frame and writes only the needed updates"
- **Textual**: "marks that widget as 'dirty' and automatically refreshes its content" 
- **Ink**: Has \`incrementalRendering\` mode that "only updates changed lines"

## Proposed Solution

1. **Use existing contentDirty flag**: Already set by reconciler when content changes
2. **Add layoutDirty flag**: Set when computed layout differs from previous
3. **Cache rendered output per node**: Store node's buffer region after first render
4. **Skip unchanged nodes**: In contentPhase, if !contentDirty && !layoutDirty, blit cached content

```typescript
function renderNodeToBuffer(node, buffer) {
  // Fast path: unchanged node
  if (!node.contentDirty && !node.layoutDirty && node.cachedContent) {
    buffer.blit(node.cachedContent, layout.x, layout.y)
    return
  }
  
  // Slow path: render and cache
  const rendered = renderNodeContent(node)
  node.cachedContent = rendered
  buffer.blit(rendered, layout.x, layout.y)
  node.contentDirty = false
  node.layoutDirty = false
}
```

## Expected Impact

- Current: 6668 nodes × 31µs = 210ms
- With caching: 2 changed nodes × 31µs + 6666 blits × ~1µs ≈ 7ms
- **30x improvement** for typical cursor movements

## Complexity

Medium-high:
- Cache invalidation when ancestors resize
- Memory overhead for cached content
- Need to handle scroll offset changes
- Clipping interaction with cached regions

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Reduce node count** (DONE - reduced depth from 2→1, 78% improvement)
2. **Line-level diffing in outputPhase** (already done, but contentPhase is the bottleneck)
3. **Virtualization** (already done via VirtualList, but doesn't help contentPhase)

## References

- Textual: https://textual.textualize.io/guide/reactivity/
- Ratatui diffing: https://github.com/ratatui-org/ratatui/discussions/579
- Ink incrementalRendering: https://github.com/vadimdemedes/ink#render-options
close_reason: Implemented incremental content rendering for scroll container children. Added prevOffset tracking to scrollState. When scroll offset is unchanged, children use the fast-path (skip re-rendering clean subtrees). 7 new tests verify correctness. Expected ~30x improvement for cursor movements within visible viewport.

title: Incremental rendering: ghost pixels when components unmount/overlay
description:
When components unmount (dialogs, toasts) or overlay existing content, the incremental rendering content phase doesn't correctly clear stale pixels from the previous buffer.

## Root cause
renderNormalChildren() iterates only current node.children — removed nodes' pixels are never cleared. Additionally, Text nodes read bg via getCellBg from the buffer, so stale background colors from previous frames leak through.

## Evidence
- INKX_CHECK_INCREMENTAL=1 crashes immediately on first keypress in km view (toast ghost at row 14)
- 4 test failures when checkIncremental enabled in testEnv: search-dialog, inline-edit, board-features, cursor-perf
- td dialog (km-qaco9): dialog closes in state but ghost remains on screen (production createApp path only)

## Affected tests (opted out with checkIncremental: false)
- cursor-perf.slow.test.tsx:123
- search-dialog.test.ts:184  
- inline-edit.spec.ts:1107
- board-features.spec.ts:283

## Fix direction
In content-phase.ts renderNormalChildren(): when childrenDirty=true, track previously-existing children's rects and clear them. Also ensure overlay components (dialogs, toasts) properly clear underlying buffer bg on mount/unmount.
close_reason: Fixed: Text bg inheritance decoupled from buffer state. renderGraphemes now uses explicit inheritedBg from findInheritedBg() instead of getCellBg(). Also clips clearNodeRegion to ancestor bounds. Test: re-enabled checkIncremental on 3 tests (search-dialog, board-features, cursor-perf). Commit: 27c695c (inkx), c4fc95ec (km).

title: inkx: inline mode cursor positioning drifts upward during streaming updates
description:
## Summary

When using inkx's inline render mode (mode: "inline") with streaming updates (useSyncExternalStore + flush()), the rendered output becomes garbled as content height grows. The summary/status line renders progressively higher on screen, overlapping with dots output.

## Reproduction

Run the dotz reporter in streaming mode:
```bash
bun run test:dotz
```

The dots section renders roughly correctly, but the summary line (and package table, slow tests) drift upward with each incremental update, causing garbled overlapping text.

## Root Cause Analysis

In `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/pipeline/output-phase.ts`, the `changesToAnsi()` function for inline mode:

1. Computes `maxY = Math.max(...changes.map(c => c.y))` — the furthest row with changes
2. Moves cursor UP by `maxY` lines: `\x1b[${maxY}A`
3. Then renders changes relative to that position

The assumption is that the cursor is at the bottom of the render region. But when content height increases between frames (new categories/files/dots appear), the cursor position assumption breaks — the cursor-up distance is wrong, causing upward drift.

## Why Tests Don't Catch This

- `dotz-streaming.test.tsx` only checks `chunks.length` increases after flush, not cursor positioning
- `createRenderer` from inkx/testing uses fullscreen buffer rendering, not inline mode
- No existing inkx tests exercise inline mode incremental rendering

## Needed

1. Fix cursor tracking in inline mode to account for height changes between frames
2. Add inline mode tests that verify cursor positioning across frames with growing content
3. Consider a test utility that captures cursor movement sequences and validates final screen state

## Related

- km-inkx-stale (stale pixel bugs in incremental rendering)
- km-jmxuh (output-phase ANSI diff stale backgrounds)
notes: User observation: dots section renders on approximately the correct lines, but the summary/status line (and sections below dots) render progressively higher with each flush. The entire non-dots section crawls upward, eventually overlapping with the dots output. This suggests the cursor-up calculation is correct for the top of the region but the height delta between frames is not being accounted for when positioning the lower sections.
close_reason: Fixed: cursor-up in changesToAnsi() now uses findLastContentLine(prev) instead of maxY of changes, and repositions cursor to findLastContentLine(next) after rendering. Added 5 tests covering growth, shrink, stable height, single-line prev, and multi-frame cursor tracking.

title: Inline mode rendering corruption when switching sections (storybook)
description:
## Problem

Running `bun storybook` (inline mode) reveals rendering corruption when switching sections with j/k. Content from the previous section bleeds through, the header doesn't fully clear, and visual artifacts appear where new content is shorter than old content.

## Root Cause

inkx inline mode (`mode: 'inline'`) uses relative cursor positioning (`\n` to move down, `\x1b[NA` to move up) and re-renders in place. Two issues:

1. **Buffer height capped at `stdout.rows`** (scheduler.ts:410) — content taller than the terminal is clipped at the buffer level, even though inline mode's output mechanism can handle taller content via newlines
2. **Incomplete clearing** — when switching from a tall section to a short one, leftover lines from the previous render are not erased

## Reproduction

```bash
bun storybook           # inline mode (default)
# Press j/k to switch sections — observe artifacts
bun storybook --fullscreen  # fullscreen mode works correctly
```

## Scope

Two sub-tasks:
1. **Fix inline re-render clearing**: When content shrinks, erase leftover lines below new content
2. **Allow inline buffer taller than terminal**: For content that exceeds stdout.rows, the buffer should grow (or use a virtual viewport)

## Files

- `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/scheduler.ts` — buffer height = stdout.rows
- `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/pipeline/output-phase.ts` — changesToAnsi inline mode, bufferToAnsi
- `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/render.tsx` — RenderOptions, mode handling
notes: Partially fixed: buffer height uncapped, leftover erasure, scrollback offset tracking + simplified to full re-render. TTY testing shows remaining corruption — scrollback lines not fully accounted for. User investigation: resetAfterCommit triggers scheduleRender during unmount; cursor show IS emitted (confirmed via xxd); may be Ghostty-specific or sync-update-wrapping issue.
close_reason: Fixed: cap inline output to terminal height (termRows). Content taller than terminal pushes lines into scrollback where cursor-up can't reach. bufferToAnsi/inlineFullRender now accept maxRows param, scheduler passes stdout.rows. Verified in TTY storybook: j/k navigation clean, no artifacts.

title: InputLayerProvider: isolate embedded component input from parent
description: When embedding interactive components (e.g., in a storybook viewer), the embedded component's useInput handlers fire simultaneously with the parent's. j/k in the parent navigates AND triggers the embedded component. Need a way to isolate input: focus mode where only the embedded component receives input, with a parent-level intercept (e.g., Escape) to unfocus. InputLayerProvider could support this with a 'disabled' prop or input routing.
close_reason: Implemented: InputBoundary component with 13 tests. Isolates embedded component input.

title: useInput state updates from child components don't trigger render flush
description: When a child component (e.g. TextArea) receives input via useInput and updates parent state via onChange callback, React's concurrent scheduler defers the commit. inkx's onCommit → scheduleRender never fires, so the frame isn't rendered. Workaround: parent must also update state in its own useInput handler. Fix: force React to flush pending work after emitting input events (flushSync or reconciler.flushSyncWork after eventEmitter.emit).
close_reason: Fixed: wrapped eventEmitter.emit in runWithDiscreteEvent() + flushSyncWork() so React commits synchronously. Root cause: getCurrentEventPriority returned DefaultEventPriority (16) for input events, letting concurrent mode defer commits indefinitely. Fix sets DiscreteEventPriority (2) during input handling.

description:
DOM-level mouse events for inkx — React DOM parity.

## Phases

### Phase 1: Mouse Events Core (inkx)
1. Add mouse event props to BoxProps/TextProps (onClick, onDoubleClick, onMouseDown/Up, onMouseMove, onMouseEnter/Leave, onWheel)
2. Tree-based hit testing (DFS walk of InkxNode screenRect, last-sibling-wins, overflow:hidden clipping)
3. Synthetic event dispatch (InkxMouseEvent mirroring React.MouseEvent, bubbling from target to root)
4. Double-click detection (300ms/2-cell default, configurable)
5. Scroll container default behavior (VirtualList + overflow:scroll handle onWheel, auto-stopPropagation when scrolled)
6. mouseenter/mouseleave (no bubble, track hover transitions)
7. Testing API (app.click(x,y), app.wheel(x,y,delta), app.doubleClick(x,y))

### Phase 2: Link Component (inkx)
1. <Link href="..."> component (wraps Text + sets OSC 8 hyperlink + registers onClick)
2. LinkHandlerProvider context (scheme → handler registry, like Electron protocol)
3. Default onClick dispatches to scheme handler (preventDefault skips navigation)
4. Unknown scheme handling (warn in dev, no-op in prod)
5. Mouse cursor shape on hover (OSC 22 for Kitty terminals)

### Phase 3: Semantic Entity Components (km-tui)
1. <Tag name="..."> — renders #name with tag color, links to km://tag/name
2. <User name="..."> — renders @name with user color, links to km://user/name

4. <NodeRef id title> — renders title as link, links to km://node/id

6. km:// scheme handler registration at app startup
7. Storybook entries for all entity components
8. Markdown renderer integration (auto-convert @mentions, #tags, [links] to entity components)

### Phase 4: Keyboard Events (future, deferred)

title: feat(inkx): Scrollback mode for ergonomic CLI output
description:
# Scrollback Mode for inkx

Ergonomic pi-tui-like experience where historical output accumulates in terminal scrollback while active UI updates in place.

## Problem Statement

Current inkx modes:
- **Fullscreen**: Alternate screen buffer, NO scrollback
- **Inline**: Normal screen buffer, scrollback EXISTS but unused

Neither provides the pi-tui pattern where users can scroll up to review history with native terminal features.

## Key Insight: No New Mode Needed

Terminal buffer model:
- **Normal screen** (inline mode) → HAS scrollback
- **Alternate screen** (fullscreen mode) → NO scrollback

Apps in inline mode can ALREADY leverage scrollback. We just need a **Freeze API** to mark content as frozen/permanent.

## Research Summary

| Framework | Approach | Scrollback |
|-----------|----------|------------|
| pi-tui | Retained-mode, line-by-line | Native terminal (gold standard) |
| Textual | Inline mode | Above viewport |
| Rich | Live + console separation | Via live.console |
| Ink/inkx | Alternate screen | None |

### Technical Findings

- **CSI 2026** (synchronized output) prevents flicker - all modern terminals support
- **DECSTBM scroll regions** buggy in Kitty/iTerm2 - avoid
- **ESC[2J]** clears visible screen only (preserves scrollback)
- **ESC[3J]** clears entire scrollback buffer (destructive)
- **Ink's `<Static>`** is NOT terminal scrollback - it's render-once but still in alternate screen

## API Options Explored

### Option 1: Separate FrozenList Component

```tsx
<FrozenList
  items={results}
  renderItem={(result, index) => (
    <Text color={result.passed ? "green" : "red"}>
      {result.passed ? "✓" : "✗"} {result.name}
    </Text>
  )}
/>
```

Pros: Clear separation of concerns
Cons: Another component to learn, diverges from VirtualList

### Option 2: VirtualList with `freeze` prop (PREFERRED)

Key insight: Both VirtualList and freeze handle items that don't fit on screen:
- VirtualList: overflow **downward** → virtualize with placeholders
- Freeze: overflow **upward** → push to terminal scrollback

```tsx
// Normal virtualization (current)
<VirtualList
  items={cards}
  height={20}
  overflow="scroll"  // default
  renderItem={...}
/>

// Freeze mode (new)
<VirtualList
  items={results}
  height={5}         // active region size
  overflow="freeze"  // or just `freeze` prop
  renderItem={...}
/>
```

| Aspect | `overflow="scroll"` | `overflow="freeze"` |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Items above viewport | Placeholder box | In terminal scrollback |
| Items below viewport | Placeholder box | In React tree (pending) |
| Memory | Only visible items | Only unfrozen items |
| User scroll | Via `scrollTo` prop | Native terminal scroll |

### Option 3: useFreeze() Hook (Imperative)

For high-frequency streaming that bypasses React reconciliation:

```tsx
const { freeze, count } = useFreeze()

useEffect(() => {
  stream.onLine((line) => {
    freeze(<Text>{line}</Text>)  // Fire-and-forget
  })
}, [])
```

## Height Options

For freeze mode, "height" means "active region size":

```tsx
// Explicit height
<VirtualList items={results} height={5} freeze renderItem={...} />

// Auto height - measure from children
<VirtualList items={results} height="auto" freeze renderItem={...} />

// No height = everything freezes immediately (pure streaming)
<VirtualList items={results} freeze renderItem={...} />

// Viewport-relative
<VirtualList items={results} height="viewport" freeze renderItem={...} />
```

## Pushing Items

Declarative (same as VirtualList):
```tsx
const [results, setResults] = useState([])
setResults(prev => [...prev, newResult])  // Component handles freezing
```

Imperative (for streaming):
```tsx
const { freeze } = useFreeze()
freeze(<Text>{line}</Text>)
```

## Implementation Layers

1. **FreezeBuffer** - tracks frozen content
2. **Term.writeToScrollback()** - semantic signal (not ANSI, just tells inkx "don't re-render this")
3. **Scheduler awareness** - skip frozen content in re-renders
4. **outputPhaseScrollback()** - new output phase with CSI 2026 wrapping

## Open Questions

1. Should `freeze` be a boolean prop or `overflow="freeze"` enum?
2. Should height be required in freeze mode or auto-detect?
3. Support both declarative (items array) AND imperative (useFreeze)?
4. Mouse wheel support in scrollback? (Terminal handles natively)

## Full Example: Test Reporter

```tsx
function TestReporter() {
  const [results, setResults] = useState<TestResult[]>([])
  const [current, setCurrent] = useState<string | null>(null)

  return (
    <Box flexDirection="column">
      {/* Results freeze to scrollback as added */}
      <VirtualList
        items={results}
        freeze
        renderItem={(r) => (
          <Text color={r.passed ? "green" : "red"}>
            {r.passed ? "✓" : "✗"} {r.name}
          </Text>
        )}
      />

      {/* Active region - always at bottom */}
      <Box>
        <Text>[{'='.repeat(progress)}] {progress}%</Text>
        {current && <Text>Running: {current}</Text>}
      </Box>
    </Box>
  )
}

// Must use inline mode (normal screen = has scrollback)
await render(<TestReporter />, term, { mode: "inline" })
```

## References

- Plan file: /Users/beorn/.claude/plans/iterative-brewing-sky.md
- pi-tui: https://mariozechner.at/posts/2025-11-30-pi-coding-agent/
- Textual inline: https://textual.textualize.io/blog/2024/04/20/behind-the-curtain-of-inline-terminal-applications/
- Rich Live: https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/stable/live.html
close_reason: Implemented: VirtualList frozen prop + useScrollback hook, 16 tests

title: Search dialog incremental render mismatch (bg=6 vs bg=0)
description:
## Problem
INKX_STRICT catches a mismatch in search-bugs.spec.ts:
- incremental: bg=6 (cyan)
- fresh: bg=0 (black/default)

Position (16, 12) in the search dialog shows stale cyan background in incremental render when it should show black.

## Analysis
- All nodes show "clean" (dirty flags already cleared after render)
- The bug is likely in dirty flag propagation when result rows change
- Result row has `backgroundColor={isSelected ? "cyan" : "black"}`
- When results filter/change, something isn't triggering proper re-render

## Related
- content-phase.ts: fast-path logic, parentRegionCleared
- host-config.ts: commitUpdate, markSubtreeDirty
- SearchDialog.tsx: result row rendering

## Workaround
Set INKX_STRICT=0 to run tests without incremental checking.
notes:
## Investigation 2026-02-05

### Fast-path fix applied
Added `!node.childrenDirty` to the fast-path check in content-phase.ts.
However, INKX_STRICT=1 still reveals mismatches at multiple positions:
- (0, 3) on renders #7, #8
- (13, 3) on renders #3, #4
- (16, 12) on renders #5, #6

### Root cause analysis
The bugs are complex - multiple factors involved:
1. Fast-path incorrectly skipping nodes when flags should prevent it
2. Region clearing not propagating correctly through deep nesting
3. Possible issues with how parentRegionCleared interacts with overflow:hidden

### Files involved
- content-phase.ts: renderNodeToBuffer fast-path logic
- renderNormalChildren: childHasPrev calculation
- host-config.ts: markSubtreeDirty propagation

### Next steps
- Add comprehensive debug logging to trace exact flag state at fast-path decision
- Create minimal reproduction for each mismatch position
- Consider refactoring fast-path to be more defensive
close_reason:
Fixed the root cause: "Bug 3" clearing code in content-phase.ts was clearing areas outside the parent's bounds.

Root cause analysis:
- When an inkx-text node inside a cyan result row (y=11, height=1) had prevLayout with height=19
- The "Bug 3" code cleared the "excess area" (y=12) using findInheritedBg (cyan from parent)
- But y=12 is OUTSIDE the parent's bounds (parent is only height=1 at y=11)
- This left stale cyan at position (16,12) in the cloned buffer

Fix in content-phase.ts:
- Added clipping of "Bug 3" clear areas to the parent's contentRect bounds
- For right margin clearing: clippedClearBottom = Math.min(rightClearBottom, parentBottom)
- For bottom margin clearing: clippedClearBottom = Math.min(bottomClearBottom, parentBottom)

This ensures we only clear areas that are within the parent's responsibility.
Areas outside the parent are the grandparent's responsibility to clear.

Tests pass with INKX_STRICT=1.

title: bug(inkx): Suspense transitions cause UI flicker — committed tree not preserved
description:
## Summary

When a React Suspense boundary suspends during a transition (e.g. triggered by useDeferredValue), inkx's terminal renderer produces frames where sibling/ancestor elements outside the Suspense boundary disappear momentarily. In React DOM, the committed tree stays visible until the new tree is ready — inkx should do the same.

## Reproduction (observed in km)

SearchDialog used useDeferredValue + Suspense to defer a synchronous SQLite query:

1. ModalDialog renders title="Search" (outside Suspense boundary)
2. User types → useDeferredValue triggers a transition
3. SearchResults component calls loader.read() which throws a promise (setTimeout(0) deferral)
4. Suspense catches it, should show fallback in results area only
5. **Bug**: The ModalDialog title disappears for ~1 frame, reappears when the promise resolves

The title is a sibling of the Suspense boundary, not inside it. React's contract: during a transition, the committed (old) UI stays visible until the new tree is fully ready. The title should never flicker.

## Workaround applied

SearchDialog was converted to synchronous rendering (dc931ad2) since the data was synchronous anyway. But this doesn't fix the underlying inkx renderer issue — real async Suspense use cases (data fetching, lazy loading) will hit the same bug.

## Investigation needed

1. **Trace the render cycle**: Add logging to inkx's reconciler/renderer to see what output is produced during a Suspense transition. Is the committed tree being discarded before the new tree is ready?
2. **Compare with react-reconciler docs**: Check how the host config's `prepareForCommit`, `resetAfterCommit`, `commitUpdate` etc. interact with Suspense transitions. The reconciler should only commit the new tree atomically.
3. **Check if inkx double-buffers**: If inkx writes output line-by-line during reconciliation (instead of buffering the full frame and swapping atomically), intermediate states would be visible as flicker.
4. **Minimal repro**: Create a test case with a simple Suspense boundary + useDeferredValue that verifies sibling content stays visible during suspension.

## Expected outcome

- Tests proving Suspense transitions don't cause sibling/ancestor flicker
- Root cause identified and fixed in the inkx renderer
- If this is a fundamental react-reconciler limitation for terminal renderers, document it and provide guidance on safe Suspense patterns
close_reason:
Root cause: All inkx createContainer() calls used LegacyRoot (0) instead of ConcurrentRoot (1).

In LegacyRoot, React degrades concurrent features — useDeferredValue, startTransition, and Suspense transitions that hold the old committed tree all behave differently. The reconciler can't preserve the old tree during transitions, causing sibling UI to flicker.

Fix: Switched all 10 createContainer calls across 8 files from LegacyRoot to ConcurrentRoot. All 1572 inkx tests and 585 km-tui tests pass with zero regressions.

Also added 8 comprehensive Suspense flicker tests covering: initial suspension, nested Suspense, multiple boundaries, state update transitions, layout shift, re-suspension, useDeferredValue+Suspense, and fixed-height containers.

title: inkx TEA runtime: focus, events, state, plugins
description: TEA-like runtime layer for inkx: externalized state store, Elm-shaped API (init/update/view/subscriptions), focus management, spatial navigation, nested scopes, key/mouse event dispatch with bubbling, plugin system. Layered as optional inkx/runtime on top of inkx/core renderer. Phase 1 delivers focus system; later phases add full TEA API, spatial nav, scroll/mouse state, plugins, and test architecture upgrade.
design:
# inkx TEA Runtime: Focus, Events, and State

## Vision

inkx gains an optional TEA runtime layer on top of its rendering core. All interaction state lives in an external store. React components are pure views reading via hooks that look like useState. Terminal events become Msgs flowing through a central update function. Apps get focus, spatial nav, scroll, and keyboard handling for free — and can override any part by handling the Msg first.

## Package Layering

The TEA runtime is NOT baked into the renderer. It's a composable layer on top, following the pattern of Flutter (widgets layer over dart:ui), Unity (EventSystem as component, not engine built-in), and SwiftUI (focus as modifier, not layout engine concern).

Three layers, each independently useful:

```
inkx/core  (PURE — zero dependencies)
  Types: Model, Msg, Cmd, Sub
  Reducer signatures, plugin composition helpers
  Testable without React, without a store, without a terminal
  ─── used by ───
inkx/store  (RUNTIME — holds state, executes effects)
  createStore(): concrete store wiring the TEA loop
  Dispatches Msgs, executes Cmds, manages Subs
  Swappable implementation (Zustand, Jotai, custom)
  ─── used by ───
inkx/react  (HOOKS — React integration)
  Hooks (useFocusable, useScroll, etc.)
  Default wiring (click-to-focus, Tab nav, spatial nav)
  run() entry point, createApp() compat wrapper
  ─── imports from ───
inkx  (RENDERER — the existing package)
  React reconciler, node tree, flexx layout,
  terminal output, cell diffing, hit testing
```

Five usage levels (pick any):

```ts
// 1. Renderer only — render to terminal, handle everything yourself
import { render } from 'inkx'
render(<App />, terminal)

// 2. Pure TEA — write reducers and test without React
import { type InkxModel, type InkxMsg, inkxUpdate, compose } from 'inkx/core'
const [model, cmds] = inkxUpdate(msg, model, ctx) // pure function

// 3. Store — TEA loop with state, without React hooks
import { createStore } from 'inkx/store'
const store = createStore({ init, update })
store.dispatch({ type: 'focus', nodeId: 'card-1' })

// 4. Full runtime — TEA + React hooks + defaults (recommended)
import { run } from 'inkx/react'
run({ init, update, view, subscriptions })

// 5. Progressive — renderer + cherry-picked TEA features
import { render } from 'inkx'
import { createFocusManager } from 'inkx/react/focus'
import { createStore } from 'inkx/store'
```

**Why separate inkx/core from inkx/store?**
- Pure reducer tests run instantly — no React, no store, no terminal
- Store implementation is swappable (Zustand today, custom tomorrow)
- Plugin authors import from inkx/core for types, never depend on store internals
- Framework-agnostic: inkx/core + a web store = same TEA logic in react-dom

**Exports by package:**

| Package | Exports |
|---------|---------|
| `inkx` | render, Box, Text, InkxNode, hitTest, getAncestorPath (renderer) |
| `inkx/core` | types (InkxModel, InkxMsg, Cmd, Sub), inkxUpdate, compose, built-in plugin functions |
| `inkx/store` | createStore, StoreApi |
| `inkx/react` | run, hooks (useFocusable, useScroll, etc.), default wiring |

`inkx` root re-exports all for convenience.

## TEA API (Elm-named)

```ts
run<Model, Msg>({
  init:          (ctx) => [Model, Cmd[]]
  update:        (msg: Msg, model: Model, ctx: Ctx) => [Model, Cmd[]]
  view:          () => JSX.Element
  subscriptions: (model: Model) => Sub[]
})
```

inkx provides InkxModel (focus, scroll, mouse, window, nodeState) and inkxUpdate as defaults. Apps extend both, handle their Msgs first, fall through to inkxUpdate.

**Replaces Layer 3 (createApp with Zustand)** — not a 4th layer. During migration, createApp() wraps the TEA API internally. Eventually deprecated.

### Type Composition (how apps extend)

```ts
// App defines its own model and msg types, extending inkx's
type AppModel = InkxModel & {
  mode: 'normal' | 'insert' | 'visual'
  board: { columns: Column[]; selectedCardId: string | null }
  search: { query: string; matches: string[] }
}

type AppMsg = InkxMsg
  | { type: 'select-card'; cardId: string }
  | { type: 'toggle-mode'; mode: AppModel['mode'] }
  | { type: 'search'; query: string }

// App update handles its own Msgs, falls through to inkxUpdate
function update(msg: AppMsg, model: AppModel, ctx: Ctx): [AppModel, Cmd[]] {
  switch (msg.type) {
    case 'select-card': return [{ ...model, board: { ...model.board, selectedCardId: msg.cardId } }, []]
    case 'toggle-mode': return [{ ...model, mode: msg.mode }, []]
    default: return inkxUpdate(msg, model, ctx)  // fall through to built-in handling
  }
}
```

### Store API

```ts
interface StoreApi<Model, Msg> {
  getModel(): Model
  dispatch(msg: Msg): void
  subscribe(listener: (model: Model) => void): () => void  // returns unsubscribe
  // Selector-based subscription (for useSyncExternalStore)
  getSnapshot<T>(selector: (model: Model) => T): T
}

function createStore<Model, Msg>(config: {
  init: (ctx: Ctx) => [Model, Cmd[]]
  update: (msg: Msg, model: Model, ctx: Ctx) => [Model, Cmd[]]
  subscriptions?: (model: Model) => Sub[]
}): StoreApi<Model, Msg>
```

Store executes Cmds synchronously after each update (batch, dispatch, terminal-write) or schedules them (schedule). If a Cmd dispatches another Msg, it's queued and processed after the current update completes — no re-entrant dispatch.

## The Update Pipeline

Terminal event arrives. Two systems need to process it:

1. **TEA update** (centralized) — app-level routing, mode switching, command system
2. **Tree dispatch** (decentralized) — onKeyDown/onFocus/onBlur props on individual nodes, with bubbling

Resolution: TEA update runs first. It can handle the Msg fully (return new model + cmds), OR it can let inkxUpdate handle it. inkxUpdate dispatches to the tree (onKeyDown with bubbling), then applies defaults (Tab → focus-next, etc.) if nothing called stopPropagation.

```
Terminal stdin
    │
    ▼
  Msg created (e.g., { type: 'term:key', key: 'j', ... })
    │
    ▼
  app update(msg, model, ctx)     ← handle or fall through
    │
    ▼
  inkxUpdate(msg, model, ctx)     ← built-in plumbing:
    ├── 1. Dispatch to tree         (onKeyDown bubbles from focused node to root)
    ├── 2. If not stopped:          apply defaults (Tab → focus-next, arrows → spatial nav)
    └── 3. Return [newModel, cmds]
    │
    ▼
  [new Model, Cmd[]]
    │           │
    ▼           ▼
  React       Cmd executor
  re-renders  (terminal write, timers, etc.)
```

This means onKeyDown props still work (React-style, decentralized) but they run INSIDE inkxUpdate as part of the tree dispatch step. The TEA update has first say, tree dispatch has second say, defaults have last say.

**Click-to-focus timing**: Fires on mousedown (not click), matching DOM behavior.

**Mode-aware routing**: If `model.mode === 'textEditing'`, the app's update should skip global shortcuts and let the text input's onKeyDown handle it.

## Event Bubbling Within inkxUpdate

When inkxUpdate dispatches a key event to the tree:

1. Build ancestor path from focused node to root
2. Capture phase: root → target (onKeyDownCapture props)
3. Target phase: focused node's onKeyDown
4. Bubble phase: parent → root (onKeyDown props)
5. Check event.propagationStopped and event.defaultPrevented
6. If not stopped/prevented: apply default behavior (Tab, arrows, etc.)

Bubbling callbacks can dispatch to the store:

```tsx
<Box focusable onKeyDown={(e, dispatch) => {
  if (e.key === 'Enter') {
    dispatch({ type: 'activate-card', cardId: myId })
    e.stopPropagation()
  }
  // Unhandled keys bubble up to parent, then to defaults
}}>
```

## Model Structure

```ts
// Provided by inkx (apps extend this)
type InkxModel = {
  focus: {
    activeId: string | null
    previousId: string | null
    origin: 'keyboard' | 'mouse' | 'programmatic' | null
    scopeStack: string[]          // nested scope IDs, outermost first
    scopeMemory: Record<string, string>  // scopeId → last focused child ID
  }
  scroll: Record<string, { x: number; y: number }>
  mouse: {
    hoverTarget: string | null
    pressed: { nodeId: string; button: number } | null
  }
  window: { cols: number; rows: number }
  nodeState: Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>  // generic per-node state
  nodes: {                        // registry — populated by useFocusable on mount
    focusable: Set<string>
    scopes: Set<string>
  }
}
```

**Changes from v1:**
- Added `scopeMemory` — stores last-focused-child per scope. When re-entering a scope, focus restores where you left off (like Flutter's FocusScopeNode).
- `hoverTarget` only (not raw x/y) — model only updates when hover target changes.

**Write-through**: After each reducer step, tree properties (node.focused, doc.activeElement) are synced. Reducer state is source of truth for snapshots/replay. Tree properties are read cache.

**React integration**: All hooks use `useSyncExternalStore` under the hood — prevents tearing in concurrent React, ensures selective re-renders.

## Msg Types

```ts
type InkxMsg =
  // Terminal events (from stdin/signals)
  | { type: 'term:key'; key: string; input: string; ctrl: boolean; meta: boolean; shift: boolean; eventType?: 1|2|3 }
  | { type: 'term:mouse'; action: 'down'|'up'|'move'|'scroll'; x: number; y: number; button: number }
  | { type: 'term:resize'; cols: number; rows: number }
  // Focus actions
  | { type: 'focus'; nodeId: string; origin?: FocusOrigin }
  | { type: 'blur' }
  | { type: 'focus-next' }
  | { type: 'focus-prev' }
  | { type: 'focus-direction'; direction: 'up'|'down'|'left'|'right' }
  | { type: 'scope-enter'; scopeId: string }
  | { type: 'scope-exit' }
  // Scroll actions
  | { type: 'scroll'; nodeId: string; x?: number; y?: number }
  | { type: 'scroll-into-view'; nodeId: string }
  // Node lifecycle
  | { type: 'node-register'; nodeId: string; focusable?: boolean; scope?: boolean }
  | { type: 'node-unregister'; nodeId: string }
  // Node state
  | { type: 'set-node-state'; nodeId: string; key: string; value: unknown }
  // Layout feedback (from flexx, after render)
  | { type: 'layout-computed'; nodeId: string; rect: Rect; contentSize: Size; viewportSize: Size }
```

## Cmd Types (Effects)

```ts
type InkxCmd =
  | { type: 'none' }
  | { type: 'batch'; cmds: InkxCmd[] }
  | { type: 'dispatch'; msg: Msg }              // dispatch another Msg next tick
  | { type: 'terminal-write'; data: string }     // raw terminal escape sequence
  | { type: 'schedule'; delayMs: number; msg: Msg }  // delayed Msg
```

## Sub Types (Subscriptions)

```ts
function subscriptions(model: Model): Sub[] {
  return [
    onKey(),                                    // always: keyboard input
    onMouse(),                                  // always: mouse events
    onResize(),                                 // always: terminal resize
    model.mode === 'insert' ? onTick(500) : null,  // conditional: cursor blink
  ]
}
```

## Ctx (Read-Only Context for update)

```ts
type Ctx = {
  layout: {
    get(nodeId: string): Rect | null
    contentSize(nodeId: string): Size | null
    viewportSize(nodeId: string): Size | null
  }
  node(nodeId: string): InkxNode | null
  tree: InkxNode
  dispatchToTree(event: InkxEvent): void
}
```

## Hooks (Look Like useState)

```tsx
// All backed by the external store via useSyncExternalStore.
const { focused, focusOrigin } = useFocusable()
const { activeElement, focus, focusNext } = useFocusManager()
const hasFocus = useFocusWithin('detail-pane')
const [scrollY, setScroll] = useScroll()
const [value, setValue] = useNodeState('query', '')
const { cols, rows } = useWindow()
```

## Spatial Navigation

Arrow keys find nearest focusable neighbor using layout positions from Ctx. Scoped to current focus scope.

```ts
case 'focus-direction': {
  const scope = currentScope(model)
  const from = ctx.layout.get(model.focus.activeId)

  // 1. Check explicit overrides first (nextFocusDown etc.)
  const explicit = getExplicitFocusLink(ctx, model.focus.activeId, msg.direction)
  if (explicit) return [focusModel(model, explicit, 'keyboard'), [scrollIntoView(explicit)]]

  // 2. Spatial search: 45° cone heuristic (tvOS-style)
  const candidates = model.nodes.focusable
    .filter(id => isInScope(id, scope, ctx))
    .map(id => ({ id, rect: ctx.layout.get(id) }))
    .filter(c => c.rect && isInCone(from, c.rect, msg.direction, 45))
  const nearest = pickNearest(from, candidates, msg.direction)
  if (nearest) return [focusModel(model, nearest, 'keyboard'), [scrollIntoView(nearest)]]

  // 3. No candidate: do nothing (no wrap)
  return [model, []]
}
```

Override with explicit links: `<Box focusable nextFocusDown="save-btn" />`

## Nested Focus Scopes

Nodes can be both focusable AND a focusScope. Enter descends, Escape ascends.

scopeStack tracks nesting: ['board', 'card-5']. Spatial nav scoped to innermost.

**Scope memory**: Last focused child saved per scope in `scopeMemory`. Re-entering restores focus.

## State Ownership Gradient

**Fully externalized (recommended)**: All interaction state via hooks. Gets: replay, snapshots, spatial nav, scroll-into-view, plugins, devtools.

**Partially externalized**: inkx plumbing in store, app state in useState. Gets: nav/focus/scroll work. Loses: full replay, plugin access to app state.

**Fully local (opt-out)**: All state in useState. Effectively a dumb renderer.

Rule: if inkx needs to know about it, it goes in the store.

## Plugin System (SlateJS-inspired)

Update middleware: `(innerUpdate) => (msg, model, ctx) => [Model, Cmd[]]`

**Ordering rule**: Outermost = highest priority. Not calling `innerUpdate` swallows the Msg.

### Built-in Plugins (composed into inkxUpdate)

| Plugin | Msg Types | What It Does |
|--------|-----------|--------------|
| `withTreeDispatch` | `term:key`, `term:mouse` | Dispatches events to tree with capture/bubble |
| `withFocusNavigation` | `focus-next`, `focus-prev` | Tab/Shift+Tab cycling |
| `withSpatialNavigation` | `focus-direction` | Arrow key nearest-neighbor (45° cone) |
| `withScopeManagement` | `scope-enter`, `scope-exit` | Enter/Escape scope transitions + scopeMemory |
| `withClickToFocus` | `term:mouse` (down) | Click focuses nearest focusable ancestor |
| `withScrollIntoView` | `focus`, `focus-direction` | Auto-scroll focused element into viewport |
| `withFocusRestore` | `node-unregister` | Restore focus when node unmounts |
| `withAutoFocus` | `node-register` | Focus autoFocus nodes on mount |
| `withMouseCapture` | `term:mouse` (move/up) | Route moves to pressed node during drag |
| `withHoverTracking` | `term:mouse` (move) | Update hoverTarget on hover changes |
| `withWindowResize` | `term:resize` | Update window dimensions |

Default composition:

```ts
const inkxUpdate = compose(
  withTreeDispatch, withFocusNavigation, withSpatialNavigation,
  withScopeManagement, withClickToFocus, withScrollIntoView,
  withFocusRestore, withAutoFocus, withMouseCapture,
  withHoverTracking, withWindowResize, baseUpdate,
)
```

### App-Level Plugins (illustrative — not all will be built)

These examples show the *kinds* of things the plugin system enables. Actual plugins will be built as needed.

| Plugin | What It Does |
|--------|--------------|
| `withCommandSystem(commands)` | Keybinding routing via command registry + mode/context/when |
| `withVimMode` | Normal/insert/visual modes. j/k → focus-direction, i → insert, Esc → normal |
| `withChordInput` | Multi-key sequences (a# → add heading). Partial chord state in model |
| `withSearchHighlight` | / opens search, match highlighting as user types |
| `withTextEditing` | Text input: cursor, selection, delete/backspace in insert mode |
| `withUndoRedo` | Undo/redo stack. Snapshots model slices on significant actions |
| `withClipboard` | Copy/paste via OSC 52 terminal sequences |
| `withDragAndDrop` | Drag items between containers using mouseCapture + drop zones |
| `withTooltips` | Contextual hints on hover/focus after delay |
| `withBreadcrumbs` | Navigation path from scope stack |
| `withHistory` | Back/forward navigation between views |
| `withAnimations` | Scheduled state changes (cursor blink, slide-in, fade) |
| `withSelectionRange` | Shift+click/arrow multi-select |
| `withColumnResize` | Drag column borders. Mouse capture + layout feedback |
| `withContextMenu` | Right-click / Shift+F10 context menu at focused node |

### Developer/Debug Plugins

| Plugin | What It Does |
|--------|--------------|
| `withDebugOverlay` | Focus state, event flow, scope stack, model inspector |
| `withReplay` | Record all Msgs, replay for debugging/snapshot tests |
| `withPersistence` | Save/restore model state across sessions |
| `withPerformanceMonitor` | Update latency, render counts, re-render detection |
| `withEventLogger` | Log every Msg with timestamp, handler, outcome |

### SlateJS Integration

km-tui uses SlateJS-style rich text editing in the detail pane. Slate has its own plugin model (editor transforms, normalizers, rendering). The two systems compose naturally:

**Boundary**: TEA handles focus/navigation/layout. Slate handles text editing within a focused editor node. The handoff is `onKeyDown` — when a focusable Slate editor node receives a key event via TEA dispatch, it feeds it to Slate's event handling. Unhandled keys bubble back up through TEA.

```
TEA plugin stack (outer)
  withCommandSystem → routes shortcuts (Cmd+B → bold)
  withTreeDispatch → dispatches to focused node
    └─ Slate editor (inner)
        Slate plugin stack: normalizers, decorations, void elements
        Handles: typing, selection, formatting
        Bubbles: Escape, Tab, unhandled shortcuts
```

**Shared model**: Slate's Value lives inside TEA Model as a slice. Slate transforms dispatch TEA Msgs that update the slice. This gives TEA full visibility — undo/redo, replay, persistence all work across both text editing and structural navigation.

**Plugin mapping**: A Slate plugin (e.g., markdown shortcuts, @mentions) is purely about text transforms. A TEA plugin (e.g., withTextEditing) is about routing and lifecycle. They don't overlap — they compose at the boundary.

## Performance (thousands of items)

Target: 1000+ focusable nodes (e.g., a board with 50 columns × 20 cards). Every hot path must be sublinear or constant-time.

### Hot Path Analysis

| Operation | Naïve Cost | Mitigation | Target |
|-----------|-----------|------------|--------|
| **Spatial navigation** (arrow keys) | O(n) scan all focusable | Spatial index (R-tree or grid). Rebuild on layout change, query O(log n) | <1ms |
| **Tab navigation** | O(n) DFS for tab order | Cache tab order, invalidate on tree mutation | <1ms |
| **Key dispatch** (focused → root) | O(depth) bubble | Tree depth ~10-15 even with 1000 nodes. Already fast. | <0.1ms |
| **Click hit testing** | O(n) existing tree walk | Already optimized in inkx (early exit, bounds check). Could add spatial index if needed. | <1ms |
| **Model update** (TEA reducer) | O(1) per Msg | Immer-style patches or manual immutable updates. Only touch affected slice. | <0.1ms |
| **React re-renders** | O(n) if store changes | `useSyncExternalStore` + selectors. Only components whose slice changed re-render. | <1ms |
| **Write-through sync** | O(n) if syncing all props | Delta-only: only sync changed node props. Track dirty set. | <0.1ms |
| **Focus change** | O(1) set + O(depth) events | Just pointer swap + fire focus/blur on old/new path. | <0.1ms |

### Spatial Navigation Index

The main performance concern. With 1000 focusable nodes, the 45° cone scan is O(n) per arrow press. Solution:

```ts
// Grid-based spatial index — O(1) amortized lookup
interface SpatialIndex {
  rebuild(nodes: FocusableNode[]): void   // O(n), called on layout change
  query(from: Rect, direction: Direction): FocusableNode[]  // O(k) where k = candidates in cone
}
```

Rebuild triggers: layout-computed Msg (already planned). Grid cell size tuned to typical node spacing. For 1000 nodes in a board layout, query returns ~5-20 candidates — the cone filter is trivial at that scale.

**If spatial nav is the bottleneck, we'll find a way** — the architecture doesn't depend on a specific algorithm. The plugin receives a Msg and returns focus target. Swap the internals without changing the API.

### Optimization Strategy

1. **Phase 1**: Naïve O(n) for spatial nav. Profile with realistic data.
2. **If >5ms on 1000 nodes**: Add grid-based spatial index.
3. **If still slow**: R-tree or quadtree. But unlikely — terminal UIs rarely exceed 1000 focusable nodes.

The TEA architecture actually helps performance: all state updates are centralized, so we can batch, debounce, and skip redundant work in one place. Plugins can `stopPropagation()` to short-circuit expensive chains.

## Migration Path

### Phase 1+3 (combined pilot): Focus + Spatial Nav
Prototype together on km-tui board layout. Validates core UX: Tab, arrows, Enter/Escape scopes, click-to-focus.
New: focusable, autoFocus, focusScope, onKeyDown, onFocus, onBlur props. useFocusable(), useFocusManager(), useFocusWithin(). Spatial nav with 45° cone. scopeMemory. useSyncExternalStore for all hooks.
Deprecate: useFocus, useInputLayer, InputBoundary.
km-tui: Board cards become individually focusable. Remove focusedPane + cursor from UIState.

### Phase 2: TEA Runtime Core + Package Split
Package split: inkx/core (pure) + inkx/store (runtime) + inkx/react (React).
New: run({ init, update, view, subscriptions }), full Msg/Cmd/Sub types. createStore(). inkxUpdate.
Migrate: createApp() wraps TEA internally.

### Phase 4: Scroll + Mouse + Window State
Remaining state migrated to store.
New: useScroll(), useWindow(). withMouseCapture, withHoverTracking. layout-computed feedback.

### Phase 5: Plugin Decomposition
Decompose inkxUpdate into composable plugins. App plugins: withCommandSystem, withVimMode.
Document ordering. Debug logging.

### Phase 6: Test Architecture
Pure reducer tests (inkx/core, no React). Plugin unit tests. Replay tests. Snapshot comparison.
Test pyramid inverts — most tests are instant pure functions.

## Node IDs

Every focusable node needs a stable string ID. This is the `testID` prop — already used pervasively in inkx and km-tui tests.

```tsx
<Box testID="card-42" focusable>  {/* testID doubles as focus ID */}
```

**Rules:**
- `testID` is the node's identity in the model (focus.activeId, scroll keys, nodeState keys)
- Must be unique within a scope. Duplicate testIDs in the same scope = undefined behavior
- Components that create dynamic focusable children (e.g., card list) should generate stable IDs: `card-${card.id}`
- Nodes without testID can still be focusable (assigned auto-generated IDs internally) but can't be targeted programmatically

**Why testID, not a new prop?** It's already there, already unique, already used for testing. Adding a separate `focusId` would mean two ID systems.

## Error Handling

- **Plugin throws**: Caught by the store. Error logged. The Msg is dropped (not re-dispatched). Model unchanged. This prevents a broken plugin from crashing the app.
- **update() throws**: Same as plugin — caught, logged, model unchanged. The terminal keeps rendering the last good state.
- **Cmd execution throws**: Caught by the Cmd executor. Error logged. Other Cmds in the batch still execute.
- **No silent failures**: All caught errors fire a `{ type: 'error'; error: Error; source: string }` Msg, which apps can handle (e.g., show in debug overlay). Follows km's "every error must produce visible feedback" principle.

## Edge Cases

- **Unmount races**: Proactively move focus in update handler, not in cleanup
- **Cascading unregister**: withFocusRestore walks up until valid target found
- **Stale node IDs**: Cleaned up on node-unregister. Focus/scroll/nodeState entries for unregistered nodes are garbage-collected.
- **Layout feedback loop**: layout-computed feeds scroll/nav data only, won't ping-pong
- **Concurrent React**: useSyncExternalStore handles tearing and aborted renders
- **Re-entrant dispatch**: Cmds that dispatch Msgs are queued, not processed inline. Prevents infinite loops and makes update ordering deterministic.

## Relationship to Vendor Rename

The sub-packages map directly to the future naming:

| inkx sub-package | Future name | What |
|-----------------|-------------|------|
| `inkx/core` | `termily-core` | TEA types, reducers, plugins. No React. |
| `inkx/store` | `termily-store` | Concrete store, effect execution. |
| `inkx/react` | `termily-react` | Hooks, run(), default wiring. |
| `inkx` (root) | `termily` | React reconciler, Box, Text, terminal rendering. |
| flexx | `flexily` | Layout engine. Standalone. |

inkx/core + a web store = same TEA logic powering a react-dom app.

title: VirtualColumns: framework-level horizontal+vertical virtualization with position tracking
description:
## Problem

Apps that render 2D grids of content (kanban boards, spreadsheets, dashboards) need two axes of virtualization:
1. **Horizontal**: only N columns visible at a time, off-screen columns don't render
2. **Vertical**: within each column, only visible items render (VirtualList)

Position tracking for cross-axis navigation (e.g., moving left/right to the same visual Y position) requires a registry of screen positions. When virtualization unmounts items, their registry entries must be cleaned up — otherwise stale entries corrupt position-based navigation.

Currently this is all app-level responsibility. This led to a stale registry entry bug in km-tui where unmounted cards left stale positions that corrupted cross-column navigation.

## Proposal

A generic 2D virtualization component in inkx — no domain concepts (no 'columns', 'cards', 'boards'). Just:

1. **Horizontal virtualization**: render only visible sections of a horizontal axis (like VirtualList but horizontal)
2. **Vertical virtualization per section**: compose with VirtualList for vertical axis within each section
3. **Position registry**: generic position tracking keyed by (sectionIndex, itemIndex) with auto-register on mount, auto-unregister on unmount
4. **Cross-axis navigation helpers**: findItemAtY(sectionIndex, targetY), stickyY/stickyX management

The API should be axis-agnostic where possible — the same primitives work for horizontal columns, vertical sections, or grids.

## Prior Art

- **Flutter**: SliverGrid/SliverList with viewport-based recycling
- **React Native**: FlatList/SectionList with viewability tracking
- **Android**: RecyclerView with LayoutManager (GridLayoutManager, StaggeredGridLayoutManager)
- **iOS**: UICollectionView with compositional layout (sections + items)
- **Web**: react-virtualized FixedSizeGrid/VariableSizeGrid, TanStack Virtual (any-axis virtualizer)
- **Terminal**: blessed (no virtualization), bubbletea/ratatui (manual viewport), textual (virtual list only)

## Design Research

Deep research fired — see results when available. Key questions:
- Composable primitives (VirtualHorizontal + VirtualList) vs monolithic VirtualGrid?
- How to make position registry generic without domain concepts?
- API patterns from TanStack Virtual that translate to terminal?

## Current Code (km-tui app layer — to be replaced)

- Board horizontal scroll: `apps/km-tui/src/views/Board.tsx:285` (`columns.slice`)
- Column scroll formula: `apps/km-tui/src/views/board-layout.ts` (`maxCols = floor(termWidth/35)`)
- VirtualList: `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/components/VirtualList.tsx`
- LayoutRegistry: `apps/km-tui/src/card-positions.ts`
- CardLayoutRegistrar: `apps/km-tui/src/views/CardColumn.tsx:74-122`
notes:
Phase 3: HVL refactoring. 3-layer architecture (Phase 2) committed as 60f2c69d. Now replacing manual column scrolling with HorizontalVirtualList.

Plan: 5 steps
1. Enhance HVL with renderOverflowIndicator + overflowIndicatorWidth props (pluggable custom indicators)
2. Refactor Board.tsx cards view — replace IIFE with <HorizontalVirtualList>, remove colScrollOffsetRef/effectiveMaxCols/effectiveScrollOffset/effectiveVisibleColumns
3. Refactor ColumnsView.tsx — replace manual map with HVL, simplify props (remove effectiveScrollOffset/effectiveMaxCols/effectiveVisibleColumns)
4. Clean up board-layout.ts — remove calcColumnWidths, getColumnWidth, calcEdgeBasedColumnScrollOffset (HVL handles internally)
5. Update tests

Key decisions:
- Use HVL component (not useVirtualization hook directly) — cleaner API
- Pluggable overflow indicators via renderOverflowIndicator prop — keeps custom VerticalScrollIndicator design
- Uniform expandedWidth per column (Math.floor(boardWidth / maxCols)) — simpler than remainder distribution, eliminates layout instability
- colIndex invariant preserved: HVL renderItem(item, index) where index IS actual colIndex
- scrollTo=undefined at board level freezes scroll (HVL feature)

title: renderStatic truncates text after wide characters (⚠ ☑)
description:
In renderStatic, certain wide characters (displayLength=2) cause text after spaces to be truncated.

## Reproduction

```tsx
import { renderStatic, Text } from 'inkx'

// These work (displayLength=1):
await renderStatic(<Text>☐ Task 1</Text>)  // ☐ Task 1
await renderStatic(<Text>☒ Task 1</Text>)  // ☒ Task 1

// These break (displayLength=2):
await renderStatic(<Text>⚠ Task 1</Text>)  // ⚠ Task (missing ' 1')
await renderStatic(<Text>☑ Task 1</Text>)  // ☑ Task (missing ' 1')

// But this also has displayLength=2 and WORKS:
await renderStatic(<Text>📁 Task 1</Text>)  // 📁 Task 1
```

## Analysis
- ⚠ (U+26A0) and ☑ (U+2611) have displayLength=2 per tui-measure
- Text after the first space gets truncated
- Other wide chars like 📁 work fine, so not all displayLength=2 chars affected
- May be related to specific Unicode ranges or East Asian width calculations

## Workaround
Use status icons with displayLength=1 (☐, ☒) instead of ⚠ (no-status icon)

title: InkZ: Implement overflow=scroll with automatic content virtualization
description:
## Goal

Enable scrollable containers in InkZ with zero configuration - developers just render their content.

## API

```tsx
// This just works - no virtualization config, no height estimation
<Box overflow="scroll" scrollTo={selectedIdx}>
  {items.map(item => <Card key={item.id} item={item} />)}
</Box>
```

Props:
- `overflow="scroll"` - enables scroll behavior with overflow indicators
- `overflow="hidden"` - clips without indicators
- `scrollTo={number}` - child index to keep visible (centered)

## How It Works

InkZ uses **measure-then-render**:
1. React creates all child elements
2. Yoga measures all children (fast - ~1ms for 500 nodes)
3. Calculate scroll position from `scrollTo` prop
4. Render content ONLY for visible children (skips expensive terminal strings)
5. Paint visible content to terminal

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `overflow="scroll"` enables scroll behavior
- [ ] `scrollTo={n}` keeps nth child visible (centered when possible)
- [ ] Only visible children have content rendered
- [ ] Overflow indicators show count of hidden items
- [ ] Works with variable-height children (Yoga measures)
- [ ] Performance: 500 items renders in <5ms total
- [ ] Works with keyboard navigation

title: InkZ: Implement position=sticky for scroll containers
description:
## Goal

Implement CSS-like `position: sticky` behavior for elements within scrollable containers, allowing headers, footers, or other elements to remain visible while scrolling.

## Use Cases

1. **Sticky headers**: Column headers that stay visible when scrolling a list
2. **Sticky footers**: Action bars or status lines that stay at bottom
3. **Sticky group headers**: Section headers in grouped lists (like iOS contacts)
4. **Breadcrumb trails**: Parent context that stays visible when navigating deep trees

## Proposed API

```tsx
// Sticky header at top of scroll container
<Box overflow="scroll" scrollTo={selectedIdx}>
  <Box position="sticky" top={0}>
    <Text bold>Column Header</Text>
  </Box>
  {items.map(item => <Item key={item.id} {...item} />)}
</Box>

// Sticky footer at bottom
<Box overflow="scroll" scrollTo={selectedIdx}>
  {items.map(item => <Item key={item.id} {...item} />)}
  <Box position="sticky" bottom={0}>
    <Text>Press Enter to select</Text>
  </Box>
</Box>

// Sticky group headers (multiple)
<Box overflow="scroll">
  {groups.map(group => (
    <Box key={group.id}>
      <Box position="sticky" top={0}>
        <Text bold>{group.name}</Text>
      </Box>
      {group.items.map(item => <Item key={item.id} {...item} />)}
    </Box>
  ))}
</Box>
```

## Implementation Considerations

1. **Requires overflow="scroll"**: Sticky only makes sense in scrollable containers
2. **Respects scroll viewport**: Sticky elements are positioned relative to visible area
3. **Stacking**: Multiple sticky elements should stack (e.g., nested group headers)
4. **Z-index**: Sticky elements render on top of scrolled content
5. **Performance**: Must not re-layout entire tree on scroll

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| position | "relative" \| "absolute" \| "sticky" | Positioning mode |
| top | number | Distance from top when sticky |
| bottom | number | Distance from bottom when sticky |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `position="sticky"` keeps element visible during scroll
- [ ] `top={0}` pins to top of scroll viewport
- [ ] `bottom={0}` pins to bottom of scroll viewport
- [ ] Multiple sticky elements stack correctly
- [ ] Works with `scrollTo` prop
- [ ] No layout recalculation on scroll (content-phase only)
- [ ] Example demonstrating sticky headers in a list

## Dependencies

- Requires km-inkz.10-scroll (overflow="scroll") to be implemented first
