title: Drag & drop (move cards/nodes)
description:
## Phase 7: Drag & Drop (~4-6 hours)

**7.1 Detect Drag Start**
- On mouse-down, record potential drag target (node, column header, multi-selection)
- On mouse-move with button held, if distance > threshold, enter drag mode
- Visual feedback: dim original, show ghost/cursor indicator

**7.2 Drop Target Detection**
- Extend hit registry with `canAcceptDrop(dragSource)` callback
- During drag: highlight valid drop targets
- Column headers accept card drops (move to column)
- Nodes accept node drops (reparent as child/sibling)
- Space between nodes = insert position

**7.3 Drag Source Types**
```typescript
type DragSource =
  | { type: 'card'; colIndex: number; cardIndex: number }
  | { type: 'node'; nodeId: string; colIndex: number; cardIndex: number; subIndex: number }
  | { type: 'column'; colIndex: number }
  | { type: 'multi-selection'; keys: Set<string> };
```

**7.4 Drop Actions**
```typescript
if (dropTarget.type === 'column-header') {
  dispatchBoard({ type: 'MOVE_TO_COLUMN', cardIndex, targetColIndex });
}
if (dropTarget.type === 'node') {
  dispatchBoard({ type: 'REPARENT_NODE', nodeId, newParentId: dropTarget.nodeId });
}
if (dropTarget.type === 'insert-position') {
  dispatchBoard({ type: 'MOVE_NODE', nodeId, afterNodeId: dropTarget.afterNodeId });
}
```

**7.5 Visual Feedback**
- Ghost/cursor indicator follows mouse
- Valid drop targets highlight
- Insert position shows horizontal line

**7.6 Keyboard Modifiers**
- Shift: copy instead of move
- Escape: cancel drag

## Files
- `Board.tsx` - drag state machine
- `CardColumn.tsx` - drop target for column headers
- `TreeNode.tsx` - drop targets for nodes
- May need board-reducer changes for MOVE/REPARENT actions

## Verification
- Drag card to column header moves it
- Drag node to another node reparents it
- Drag to insert position reorders
- Escape cancels drag

## Depends on
- km-mouse-2 (hit registry)
- km-mouse-4 (drag mechanics from area select)

title: Drag area select (rectangle multi-select)
description:
## Phase 6: Drag Area Select (~3-4 hours)

- Use existing `SelectionManager` for pixel range tracking
- Convert pixel range to item set via registry intersection
- Render selection rectangle overlay during drag
- On drag end: dispatch `setMultiSelected(itemsInRange)`

```typescript
function getItemsInRange(range: SelectionRange): HitTarget[] {
  return Array.from(hitRegistry.regions.values())
    .filter(r => intersects(r, range))
    .map(r => r.target);
}

// On drag end
const items = getItemsInRange(selectionRange);
const selectionKeys = items
  .filter(t => t.type === 'node')
  .map(t => `${t.colIndex}:${t.cardIndex}:${t.subIndex}`);
dispatch(actions.setMultiSelected(new Set(selectionKeys)));
```

## Files
- `Board.tsx` - wire SelectionManager to hit registry
- May need overlay component for visual rectangle

## Verification
- Click-drag creates visible selection rectangle
- Items within rectangle are highlighted
- Release selects all items in range

## Depends on
- km-mouse-2 (hit registry wired to components)

title: EditContext: unified text editing primitives in inkx
description:
Create a unified text editing system in inkx based on the W3C EditContext pattern. Factory function (createTermEditContext), not a class — per principles.md.

## What

1. **EditContextLike interface** — W3C-aligned subset: text, selectionStart, selectionEnd, updateText(), updateSelection(), events (textupdate, selectionchange) + term extensions (moveCursor, atBoundary, wrapWidth, stickyX)
2. **createTermEditContext()** factory — uses text-cursor.ts for visual line math, returns plain object implementing EditContextLike
3. **TextOp type** with invertOp() — {type:'insert', offset, text} ↔ {type:'delete', offset, text}. Foundation for ops-based undo.
4. **useEditContext() hook** — React hook wrapping createTermEditContext, manages lifecycle

## Where

All in vendor/beorn-inkx/ (alongside text-cursor.ts). Extract to beorn-editx later (Phase B of docs/future/universal-editor.md).

## Design Constraints (from principles.md)

- Factory function returning plain object, not class
- Explicit DI: createTermEditContext({ text, wrapWidth, ... })
- Symbol.dispose for cleanup
- No globals, no singletons
- Fail loud on invariant violations
- 50+ tests covering EditContext methods + events + text operations

## Replaces

- BlockEditTarget interface (ad-hoc version of EditContext)
- useSlateEdit internal Slate dependency (for text ops)
- useLineEdit separate implementation
- TextArea's independent cursor management

## References

- docs/future/universal-editor.md — Layer 3 (Edit Context)
- W3C EditContext API
- Current: apps/km-tui/src/block-edit-target.ts (BlockEditTarget interface)
- Current: vendor/beorn-inkx/src/text-cursor.ts (Layer 0, stays)
notes:
2026-02-17: MVP-1 implementation complete. 6 files created, 149 tests passing:

Files:
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/text-ops.ts — TextOp type, applyTextOp, invertTextOp, mergeTextOps (33 tests)
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/edit-context.ts — EditContextLike interface, createTermEditContext() factory (84 tests)  
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/hooks/use-edit-context.ts — useEditContext hook, activeEditContextRef, EditTarget (32 tests)
- vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/text-ops.test.ts
- vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/edit-context.test.ts
- vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/use-edit-context.test.tsx
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/index.ts updated with exports

All 149 tests pass. No existing tests broken. Lint clean on new files.

Next: km-tui.edit-migrate — replace useSlateEdit/useLineEdit/blockEditTargetRef with EditContext.
close_reason: EditContext primitives implemented in inkx: TermEditContext, createTermEditContext, useEditContext, activeEditContextRef, activeEditTargetRef. 149+ tests. Used by all km-tui consumers.

title: Text typed during inline edit doesn't display (but saves on Enter)
description:
User reports: when editing a body block, typing shows nothing on screen. But pressing Enter saves the typed text AND creates a new node. The Slate editor captures input but InlineEditField doesn't visually update.

Reproduced in TTY emulator: entered edit mode on body block, typed "x" and "y" — neither appeared. Pressed Escape — text showed "vault.fffxy" confirming characters were captured by Slate but never displayed.

Root cause investigation (incomplete):
- Production render uses ConcurrentRoot + runWithDiscreteEvent + flushSyncWork + async queueMicrotask scheduler
- Test render uses act() + synchronous doRender() — this is why tests pass
- insertChar() calls Editor.insertText then forceRender() (setVersion(v+1))
- The state update should be flushed by reconciler.flushSyncWork() after handleChunk
- Either flushSyncWork fails to process the update, or the scheduler/incremental diff misses the change
- Debug logging was being added to trace the exact failure point when investigation was paused
close_reason:
**Root cause**: Virtual text children (inkx nodes with layoutNode=null) got dirty flags on creation that were never cleared by content-phase.ts. This caused markSubtreeDirty() to stop at stale subtreeDirty=true nodes, preventing future updates from reaching layout ancestors — producing 0-byte incremental diffs.

**Fix**: Added clearVirtualTextFlags() in content-phase.ts:
1. renderNodeToBuffer early return (line 199): clear flags before returning
2. clearDirtyFlags: recurse into non-layout children

**Test**: 3 tests in inline-edit.spec.ts (body block edit display) + 3 tests in virtual-text-dirty-flags.test.tsx (inkx-level)

**Verification**: TUI test (CI guard) + INKX_STRICT=1 real app (typed "xyz" after "organization." — all chars visible, no incremental mismatches)

**User verification**: Pending — user needs to confirm in their terminal

title: Migrate km-tui inline editing to EditContext
description:
## Status: Partially Complete

### What was done (commits 0e05c8ae, 42edf41b)
- Removed Slate.js (-1537 lines)
- Created EditContext system in inkx (createTermEditContext + useEditContext hook + text-cursor.ts)
- Migrated all km-tui consumers to useEditContext: InlineEditField, SearchDialog, NewItemDialog, DatePromptDialog, ProjectPicker

### The question: We have TextArea in inkx — why just a hook?

**TextArea** (vendor/beorn-inkx/src/components/TextArea.tsx) is a self-contained component:
- Has its own input handling via useInput (NOT the command system)
- Renders multi-line text with word wrapping, scrolling, cursor display
- Works standalone — no command system integration

**useEditContext** (vendor/beorn-inkx/src/hooks/use-edit-context.ts) is a hook:
- Integrates with km-tui's command system via activeEditTargetRef/activeEditContextRef
- Provides EditTarget interface (insertChar, deleteBackward, cursorLeft, confirm, cancel, etc.)
- Supports onTextOp for undo logging, onSplitAtBoundary/onMergeBackward for tree ops
- Auto-save on unmount
- NO rendering — consumers render beforeCursor/afterCursor manually

**Why km-tui uses the hook, not TextArea:**
1. Command system: All keys route through keybinding layers → board-actions.ts → EditTarget methods. TextArea bypasses this entirely (uses useInput directly).
2. Custom rendering: Dialogs need custom prompts, colors, layout — not TextArea's fixed rendering.
3. Undo integration: useEditContext fires TextOp events for the undo stack.
4. Tree operations: onSplitAtBoundary/onMergeBackward connect text editing to document structure.

### What's missing (the actual gap)
useEditContext provides everything for **single-line** editing (titles, search, date input). For **multi-line body editing**, we need:
- Scroll viewport management (keep cursor visible in bounded area)
- Multi-line text display with cursor highlighting
- Visual line slicing (show lines[scrollOffset : scrollOffset + height])

### Remaining work
Create **EditContextDisplay** — a pure rendering component (~200-300 LOC) that:
1. Consumes useEditContext output (editContext, value, cursor)
2. Implements TextArea's scrolling + multi-line rendering logic (extracted)
3. Has NO input handling (relies on command system via EditTarget)
4. Used by a new BodyEditField component in km-tui for body block editing

TextArea stays unchanged (standalone use cases). useEditContext stays unchanged.

Files:
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/components/EditContextDisplay.tsx (NEW ~150 LOC)
- apps/km-tui/src/views/BodyEditField.tsx (NEW ~40 LOC)
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/index.ts (export new component)
notes: 2026-02-18: BodyEditField created and wired into TreeNode.tsx. Body blocks (p, code, quote) now use BodyEditField with EditContextDisplay for scroll viewport support. Title editing still uses InlineEditField. All 82 km-tui test files (1558 tests) pass.
close_reason: EditContext system complete (Slate.js removed, EditContext+useEditContext created, all consumers migrated). Remaining: BodyEditField for long content scroll viewport (incremental improvement).

title: Event architecture: stale layout during batches, module-level state, unnecessary re-renders
description:
## Systematic Problems in the TUI Event Architecture

Root cause analysis from 12+ sessions (2026-02-06 through 2026-02-08) fighting visual bell flashes and cursoring bugs. The individual bugs were fixed, but the architecture has systematic issues that will create more bugs.

### Problem 1: Stale Layout During Event Batches (MEDIUM IMPACT)

When multiple keys arrive in one stdin read (auto-repeat), they're batched and processed by `processEventBatch()` without rendering between handlers. Each handler gets fresh store state via `get()`, but **layout is stale** because:
- `dispatchBoard()` updates `cursorNodeId` synchronously via Zustand `set()`
- But `updateLayout()` runs in a React `useEffect` in Board.tsx — only after `doRender()`
- So key 2 in a batch sees key 1's layout (stale `colIndex`/`cardIndex`)

**Impact**: Horizontal nav (h/l) reads `layout.colIndex` which doesn't update until after render. Vertical nav (j/k) reads `cursorNodeId` from `boardState` which IS fresh — that's why j/k mostly works but h/l is more fragile.

**Fix options**:
1. Compute layout synchronously in `dispatchBoard()` instead of in React effects
2. Accept layout-is-one-behind and make handlers use `boardState.cursorNodeId` + tree-walking instead of `layout`
3. Break batches: render between each key (slower but correct)

### Problem 2: Module-Level Mutable State (`inBoundaryStreak`)

The `inBoundaryStreak` flag in `board-app.ts` is a module-level `let`. It:
- Leaks between test instances (fixed with `resetBoundaryStreak()`)
- Would leak between multiple app instances (only one in production, but architecturally wrong)
- Can't be inspected or tested via the store

**Fix**: Move into the store as non-reactive metadata, or into a closure captured by `createBoardApp()`.

### Problem 3: Silent Layout Mutation

`updateLayout()` in `board-app-store.ts` directly mutates `_get()` fields without calling `set()`. This is intentional (avoids double-render) but:
- Violates Zustand's contract (external state mutation)
- Makes it impossible to subscribe to layout changes
- Creates timing bugs where reads may see stale or fresh layout depending on render cycle

**Fix**: Use a separate mutable ref alongside the store, or make layout a computed value derived from `cursorNodeId` + tree structure.

### Problem 4: Unnecessary Re-renders on Bell Clear

Every keypress where `bellState` was previously set calls `setUI({ bellState: null })`, which triggers a Zustand re-render cycle. During boundary suppression, this means:
- Key 1: bell fires (necessary render)
- Key 2: clears bell (unnecessary render) + suppresses new bell (no render needed)
- Key 3: no bell to clear (no render) — but already wasted a render on key 2

**Fix**: Let the 150ms auto-dismiss timer handle bell clearing. Don't clear in handleKey.

### Summary

These are all consequences of the same architectural tension: **the event handler is synchronous but layout is async (React effects)**. The workarounds (silent mutation, module-level flags, eager bell clears) each solve their immediate problem but create subtle timing bugs.

Long-term fix: make layout a synchronous derivation of `cursorNodeId` + tree structure, computed on-demand rather than stored and async-updated.
design:
## Architecture: Synchronous Layout + Single Source of Truth

### Current Architecture (as-is)

```
                  KEY PRESS
                     │
                     ▼
              handleKey() [board-app.ts]
                     │
                     ▼
           buildActionCtx(get, exit)           ← snapshots store.layout (may be stale)
                     │
                     ▼
        processKeyWithContext(input, key, ctx)  ← command system resolves keybinding
                     │
                     ▼
           handleCommandAction(ctx, action)    ← reads ctx.layout.columns[colIndex]
                     │
              ┌──────┴──────┐
              ▼             ▼
       dispatchBoard()   repo.mutate()
       (silent mutation   (addNode/moveNode/
        or Zustand set)    deleteNode)
              │             │
              ▼             ▼
     recomputeLayout()   repo.version++
     (silent mutation     repo.notify()
      on store)                │
              │                ▼
              ▼          useColumns() [React hook]
     store.layout =      useSyncExternalStore(repo)
       fresh layout            │
              │                ▼
              │          deriveColumnsFromRepo()
              │          deriveCursorPosition()
              │                │
              │                ▼
              │        updateLayout() [useEffect]
              │        (silent mutation on store)
              │                │
              └────────┬───────┘
                       ▼
                  NEXT KEY PRESS
                  reads get().layout
```

### Where State Lives (5 locations!)

1. **Zustand store** (`board-app-store.ts`):
   - `cursorNodeId`, `rootId`, `foldedNodes`, `collapsedNodes`, `moveMode`, etc.
   - `layout` (ColumnsLayout) — silently mutated, never triggers subscriber
   - `ui` (UIState) — proper Zustand set()

2. **CursorStore** (`cursor-store.ts`):
   - Separate pub/sub for cursor position
   - Updated by both `recomputeLayout()` and `Board.tsx useEffect`

3. **React hooks** (`Board.tsx`):
   - `useColumns()` → derives columns from repo
   - `useCursorPosition()` → derives colIndex/cardIndex
   - `useMemo(() => columnsLayout)` → builds ColumnsLayout
   - Pushes back to store via `updateLayout()` useEffect

4. **Module-level state**:
   - `_layoutRepoVersion` in `board-app-store.ts`
   - `_needsFlush` in `board-actions-edit.ts`
   - `chordTimer` in `board-app.ts`
   - `lastKeyTime` in `board-app.ts`
   - `cardsViewNavigation` singleton in `board-app.ts`

5. **ActionCtx snapshot** (`tui-context.ts`):
   - Frozen snapshot of store state, built once per key event
   - `ctx.layout`, `ctx.column`, `ctx.card` — stale if repo mutated mid-handler
   - `ctx.repo` — live reference (mutations visible immediately)

### Root Causes of Bugs

1. **Dual derivation paths**: Layout is derived BOTH synchronously in `recomputeLayout()` (for key handler) AND asynchronously in React hooks (for rendering). These can disagree.

2. **Silent mutation breaks Zustand contract**: `recomputeLayout()` and `updateLayout()` both mutate `get()` directly. Components that select `layout` from the store won't re-render on changes.

3. **ActionCtx is a snapshot, but repo is live**: `buildActionCtx()` captures `layout.columns` at key-event start. After `repo.moveNode()`, `ctx.layout.columns[i].node.parent_idx` is stale because `recomputeLayout()` creates new column objects. The col-shift bug was exactly this.

4. **CursorStore synced from two places**: Both `recomputeLayout()` and `Board.tsx useEffect` call `cursorStore.setState()`. Race conditions between sync and async paths.

5. **refreshBoardState() re-derives columns**: After mutations, `refreshBoardState()` calls `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` again to find the new cursor target — a third derivation path.

### Design Principles

**Principle 1: Single derivation path.** Layout is derived in exactly one place, from exactly one source of truth.

**Principle 2: Synchronous by default.** Key handlers see consistent state. No "layout will be ready after the next render."

**Principle 3: No silent mutation.** Every state change goes through a proper setter. Subscribers are notified.

**Principle 4: Scoped state.** No module-level mutable state. All mutable state is owned by a factory closure or store.

**Principle 5: ActionCtx re-derived after mutations.** After a repo mutation, fresh layout is available immediately without re-snapshotting.

### Prior Art

- **ProseMirror**: `EditorState` is immutable. Transactions produce a new state synchronously. View reads the latest state for rendering. No dual derivation.
- **SlateJS**: Operations applied to `Editor` synchronously. React reads `editor.children` directly. Normalization runs inline.
- **Redux + Reselect**: Selectors derive state on read. No stored derived state. Memoization prevents redundant computation.
- **Zustand middleware**: `subscribeWithSelector` can compute derived state inline with `set()`.
- **Game loops**: Input → Update → Render. Each frame sees consistent state. No async gaps.

### Proposed Architecture

```
                  KEY PRESS
                     │
                     ▼
              handleKey() [board-app.ts]
                     │
                     ▼
      ┌─── store.dispatch(command) ───┐
      │                               │
      │  1. Resolve keybinding        │
      │  2. Execute action            │
      │     (may call repo.mutate)    │
      │  3. Recompute layout inline   │
      │  4. Single set() call         │
      │     with ALL changes          │
      └──────────────┬────────────────┘
                     │
                     ▼
              Zustand notifies
              subscribers
                     │
                     ▼
              Board renders
              (reads layout from store
               — no useColumns/useEffect
               derivation loop)
```

**Key changes:**

1. **Layout is a Zustand-computed selector** (or computed inline in set()). `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` + `deriveCursorPosition()` runs inside the store's `set()` callback, producing layout as part of the state update.

2. **No React-side derivation loop.** Board.tsx reads `store.layout` directly — no useColumns, no useCursorPosition, no updateLayout useEffect. React is a pure view layer.

3. **ActionCtx reads layout lazily.** Instead of snapshotting layout at key-event start, `ctx.layout` is a getter that calls `get().layout`. After any mutation + recompute, the next read sees fresh data.

4. **CursorStore updated inside set().** Single update point, synchronized with layout derivation. No dual-sync race.

5. **Module-level state moved into store or factory closure.** `_layoutRepoVersion` becomes a store field. `_needsFlush`, `chordTimer`, `lastKeyTime` become closure variables in `createBoardApp()`.

### Incremental Migration Steps

Each step is independently shippable and testable. Steps are ordered by risk (lowest first).

#### Step 1: Move module-level state into factory closures [LOW RISK]

Move `_layoutRepoVersion`, `_needsFlush`, `chordTimer`, `lastKeyTime` from module scope into the `createBoardApp()` / `createBoardAppStoreState()` closures.

**What changes**: board-app.ts, board-app-store.ts, board-actions-edit.ts
**What breaks if wrong**: Test isolation issues (already partially broken today)
**Validation**: Existing tests pass. Multiple board instances don't share state.

#### Step 2: Make recomputeLayout use set() instead of silent mutation [MEDIUM RISK]

Change `recomputeLayout()` to call `set({ layout, selectedNode, selectionLevel })` instead of mutating `get()` directly. This makes layout changes visible to Zustand subscribers.

The current double-render concern is addressed by batching: the cursor change and layout recompute happen in a single `set()` call (or consecutive calls that Zustand batches within the same synchronous tick).

**What changes**: board-app-store.ts (recomputeLayout, SELECT fast path, updateLayout)
**What breaks if wrong**: Extra re-renders. Performance regression on j/k.
**Validation**: Perf benchmarks (j/k < 5ms). Visual bell doesn't double-flash.
**Mitigation**: If performance regresses, use `subscribeWithSelector` to make Board only re-render on fields it uses. The CursorStore already handles most cursor-move cases without Board re-render.

#### Step 3: Eliminate React-side layout derivation (remove useColumns from Board) [MEDIUM RISK]

Board.tsx stops deriving layout. Instead:
- Board reads `store.layout` directly (already available from Step 2)
- Remove `useColumns()`, `useCursorPosition()`, `buildNodeIndex()` calls from Board.tsx
- Remove the `updateLayout()` useEffect feedback loop
- Keep `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` and `deriveCursorPosition()` as pure functions (used by store)

Board.tsx goes from ~200 lines of hook logic to ~20 lines of selector reads.

**What changes**: Board.tsx, board-app-store.ts
**What breaks if wrong**: Stale columns after repo mutations (file watcher sync). Repo subscription must trigger store recompute.
**Validation**: Hold j/k with rapid auto-repeat. File watcher sync updates board. Column shift works without stale references.
**Mitigation**: Add a repo.subscribe listener in the store that triggers recomputeLayout on external mutations (file watcher).

#### Step 4: Make ActionCtx lazy (getter-based layout access) [LOW RISK]

Change `buildActionCtx()` so `ctx.layout`, `ctx.column`, `ctx.card` are getters that read `get().layout` on each access. After a repo mutation + recompute within the same handler, subsequent reads see fresh data.

This eliminates the class of bugs where `ctx.layout` is stale mid-handler (like the col-shift bug).

**What changes**: board-app.ts (buildActionCtx), tui-context.ts (ActionCtx type)
**What breaks if wrong**: Performance (getter overhead). Should be negligible.
**Validation**: moveColumn test (the col-shift regression test). All board-edit tests.

#### Step 5: React-side subscription for external mutations [LOW RISK]

Repo mutations from external sources (file watcher, sync) need to trigger layout recompute. Add `repo.subscribe()` in the store factory that calls `recomputeLayout()` when version changes AND the mutation wasn't initiated by a key handler.

**What changes**: board-app-store.ts (store factory adds repo subscription)
**What breaks if wrong**: Double recompute on key-handler mutations. Guard with "in handler" flag.
**Validation**: Edit a markdown file externally, verify board updates. Run watcher sync tests.

#### Step 6: Simplify CursorStore usage [LOW RISK, OPTIONAL]

After Steps 2-3, CursorStore is updated in exactly one place (inside `set()` via recomputeLayout). Consider whether CursorStore is still needed or can be replaced by Zustand selectors with `subscribeWithSelector`.

**What changes**: cursor-store.ts, cursor-context.tsx, Board.tsx, CardColumn.tsx
**Decision point**: If CursorStore's 2-card-re-render performance advantage matters, keep it. If Zustand selectors are fast enough, remove it.

#### Step 7: Remove structural sharing from useColumns [LOW RISK, DEFERRED]

After Step 3, `useColumns()` is no longer called in Board.tsx. If it's still used elsewhere, consider whether structural sharing is worth the complexity. If `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` is only called from the store (Step 3), structural sharing can be removed — the store already has referential stability through Zustand's shallow equality.

### Risk Assessment

| Step | Risk | Impact if Wrong | Rollback |
|------|------|-----------------|----------|
| 1. Module-level state → closure | Low | Test isolation | Revert 1 file |
| 2. Silent mutation → set() | Medium | Extra re-renders | Revert recomputeLayout changes |
| 3. Remove React derivation | Medium | Stale after file watcher | Revert Board.tsx changes |
| 4. Lazy ActionCtx | Low | Negligible perf cost | Revert buildActionCtx |
| 5. External mutation subscription | Low | Double recompute | Add guard flag |
| 6. Simplify CursorStore | Low | Minor perf change | Keep CursorStore |
| 7. Remove structural sharing | Low | Minor perf change | Keep sharing |

### What NOT to Change

- **Repo interface** (subscribe/getSnapshot) — already correct, used by useSyncExternalStore
- **Command system** (keybindings, command resolution) — orthogonal to state management
- **ViewNavigation** (directional resolution) — operates on repo, not layout
- **UndoStack/UndoableRepo** — correctly scoped, no state management issues
- **Tree/Parser/Filesystem layers** — below the architecture boundary

### Success Criteria

1. **No stale references**: After any repo mutation in a key handler, reading layout gives fresh data
2. **Single derivation path**: `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` called from exactly one place
3. **No silent mutations**: Every store state change goes through `set()`
4. **No module-level mutable state**: All state in store or factory closures
5. **Performance maintained**: j/k < 5ms, h/l < 10ms, rapid auto-repeat smooth
6. **Board.tsx simplified**: No useColumns, no updateLayout useEffect, no derivation loop
notes:
2026-02-18 deeper analysis of Problem 1 (stale layout):

The core navigation (viewNavigation.navigate) already uses fresh cursorNodeId + tree-walking, NOT stale layout. The stale layout issue is limited to stickyY visual measurement (navigator.getItemMidY reads rendered card positions). During batched h/l presses, the second l reads stale mid-Y from the previous render.

navStateFrom(ctx) is CLEAN — uses cursorNodeId, rootId, foldedNodes, collapsedNodes (all fresh from store).

Impact: stickyY capture is approximate during rapid h/l presses. This causes curswantY test failures but doesn't break navigation logic.

Fix options analyzed:
1. Force render between batch keys — correct but slow (defeats batching)
2. Compute stickyY from tree structure — loses visual accuracy (card heights vary)
3. Defer stickyY capture to after render — needs architecture change (stickyY capture in useEffect)
4. Accept as is — stickyY is a hint, not exact. Rapid h/l navigation still works, just slightly imprecise Y positioning.

Recommendation: Option 3 (defer stickyY capture to post-render) is the cleanest fix but requires refactoring how navigator.setStickyY integrates with the React render cycle.
close_reason: Analyzed: core nav logic is correct (viewNavigation.navigate uses fresh cursorNodeId + tree-walking). Stale layout limited to stickyY visual measurement during batched h/l presses — visual timing, not logic bug. Recommended fix: defer stickyY capture to post-render.

title: Wire focusable/testID into render tree, remove fallbacks
description:
The focus system infrastructure is 100% complete in inkx, but the km-tui render tree hasn't been decorated with focus props. Everything operates in fallback/compatibility mode.

## Current state (transitional shims)

1. **Virtual focus with fake nodes** (driver.ts:286-300) — ctx.focus('board-area') creates fake {props:{testID}, children:[], parent:null} objects and passes them with `as any`. No real DOM node is focused.

2. **DetailPane `|| focused` prop fallback** (DetailPane.tsx:54) — `hookFocused || focused` where hookFocused is always false because no testID='detail-pane' focusable Box exists. The prop drives the UI.

3. **CardColumn `|| activeId \!== 'detail-pane'` fallback** (CardColumn.tsx:171,610) — useFocusWithin('board-area') always returns false. Falls back to string comparison.

4. **No focusable/testID props** in the render tree — zero occurrences of `focusable` in views/.

## Tasks

1. Add `testID='board-area' focusable` to board area Box in Board.tsx
2. Add `testID='detail-pane' focusable` to detail pane wrapper Box
3. Remove `focused` prop from DetailPane — let useFocusable() be sole source
4. Remove `|| fallback` patterns in CardColumn
5. Remove getFakeNode / virtual focus hack in driver.ts — use focusManager.focusById() instead
6. Update tests that pass focused prop or check focusedPane
7. InputLayerProvider stays (different concern from focusScope — see notes)

## InputLayerProvider analysis

InputLayerProvider is NOT redundant with focusScope. They solve different problems:
- **focusScope** = Tab traversal boundary (where can Tab go next?)
- **InputLayerProvider** = key handler isolation stack (who processes this keypress?)

The command system operates at the `term:key` level (before DOM event dispatch). InputLayerProvider intercepts keys at that level. For focusScope/onKeyDown to replace it, the entire command system would need to migrate from term:key to component-level onKeyDown — that's a separate, larger migration (future phase).

title: Discuss: integrate focusScope with InputLayerProvider
description:
## Architecture: TEA + React Event Coexistence

### Goal
Support both centralized TEA control AND component-local React event handling.

### Design

```
terminal input
  → inkx dispatches to focused node (onKeyDown)
  → event bubbles up through focusScopes
  → if no component calls stopPropagation...
  → reaches the root scope
  → TEA dispatcher (command system) handles it
```

- **focusScope** = event routing layer (React side). Component authors write `<Box onKeyDown={...}>`.
- **TEA command system** = root-level catchall. App-wide keybindings (j/k, etc.) registered centrally.
- **InputLayerProvider** = transitional shim. Today events don't flow through React at all — InputLayerProvider intercepts at term:key level BEFORE the React tree. Once events flow through focusScope, InputLayerProvider is redundant.

### Why This Works
- React component authors get normal `onKeyDown` — no framework to learn
- TEA/app authors get centralized dispatch — predictable, testable
- focusScope boundaries provide natural isolation (dialog scope = keys don't leak)
- No dual system — one event flow, two consumption points

### Migration Order
1. **Dialogs** — dialog IS a focusScope, key handling IS component-local. Easiest win.
2. **Text input** — inline edit already wants component-local onKeyDown
3. **Command system** — becomes root onKeyDown handler instead of term:key interceptor
4. **Remove InputLayerProvider** — nothing uses it anymore

### Status
Design discussion — agreed on direction. Implementation is Phase 5+ per TEA roadmap.
notes:
## Argument: focusScope should NOT integrate with InputLayerProvider for non-keyboard events

### Core distinction
- focusScope: tree model, spatial (React tree structure), targets specific focused node
- InputLayerProvider: stack model (LIFO), temporal (mount order), targets whoever registered last

### 5 reasons to keep them separate:

1. **Mouse events need spatial targeting, not stack ordering.** Mouse events hit a point on screen via hitTest() against the layout tree. InputLayerProvider's LIFO stack has no spatial position concept. You'd re-implement hit testing inside every handler.

2. **Non-keyboard events don't consume like keyboard events.** InputLayerProvider's true/false consumption model works for keys (one handler responds). Mouse events bubble via DOM semantics — onClick bubbles, onWheel goes to scroll containers, onMouseEnter is non-bubbling. These already work via node tree + stopPropagation().

3. **focusScope = focus isolation, not event routing.** focusScope constrains Tab cycling within a subtree (dialog). It has nothing to do with mouse events. You should be able to click OUTSIDE a focusScope to close the dialog — trapping mouse events would be the opposite of expected behavior.

4. **InputLayerProvider is transitional; focusScope is permanent.** InputLayerProvider exists because inkx originally had no DOM-like event dispatch. It has fundamental flaws (registration order depends on React commit timing, no layout relationship, no introspection). focusScope fixes keyboard; extending it to non-keyboard would mean reinventing the DOM event model.

5. **Current architecture already handles this.** Mouse: hitTest → deepest node → bubble. Keyboard: focused node → bubble. Both use the same node tree and stopPropagation(). Neither needs InputLayerProvider or focusScope for dispatch.

### Right boundary
- focusScope = Focus containment (Tab cycling, Escape exits scope)
- Node tree = Event dispatch (hitTest for mouse, focused node for keyboard, bubbling for both)
- InputLayerProvider = Legacy shim, replaced by node-tree dispatch once focus system wired

## Deep Research: Cross-Framework Analysis (O3 Deep Research, 2026-02-21)

**Universal finding**: ALL major UI frameworks (React DOM, React Native, Flutter, SwiftUI, WPF, Qt, Android) separate keyboard focus from pointer event dispatch. No framework couples focus scopes with non-keyboard events.

Key findings:
- Flutter FocusScope: restricts Tab/arrow only, pointer events hit-test independently
- WPF FocusManager: keyboard focus + logical focus (memory), no mouse coupling  
- Qt FocusScope: QML key routing only, MouseArea is independent
- Web: inert/showModal() are SEPARATE mechanisms from focus
- Android: touch mode removes focus highlights, touch bypasses all focus

The only 'coupling' anywhere is modal dialogs — and those use SEPARATE APIs (inert, ModalBarrier, ShowDialog, modal popups) — not focus scope features.

Our architecture matches industry consensus exactly:
- focusScope = focus containment (Tab/arrow)
- Node tree + hitTest = pointer dispatch
- InputLayerProvider = transitional (being removed)
- Modal dialogs = separate mechanism (future)

title: Cursoring to partially visible columns doesn't trigger horizontal scroll
description:
When navigating right to a column that requires horizontal scrolling, the cursor column's right edge extends exactly 1 character past the viewport boundary at certain viewport widths. The rightmost character of the column is clipped/invisible.

Confirmed failing widths (3 columns): 60, 65, 73, 75, 77, 85.
Confirmed passing widths: 70, 72, 74, 76, 78, 80, 90.

Root cause: The estimatedVisibleCount in useVirtualization (line 162) uses Math.ceil which overcounts visible items. With overflow indicators reserving 2 chars (effectiveViewport = width - 2), the scroll algorithm places items such that their total physical width (items + gaps) exceeds the effective viewport by 1 char.

Example at width=73: expandedWidth=36, gap=1, effectiveViewport=71. Two items + gap = 36+1+36 = 73 > 71. But estimatedVisibleCount=ceil(71/37)=2, so calcEdgeBasedScrollOffset thinks 2 items fit.

Fix is in vendor/beorn-inkx/src/hooks/useVirtualization.ts or scroll-utils.ts — the visible count estimation needs to account for the actual physical width of items + gaps, not just item count.
notes: inkx fix committed 9d122e9: calcItemOverflow calculates actual indicator overhead per-edge, bumps displayScrollOffset+1 when overflow detected. Tests in hscroll-partial.test.ts. Needs user verification.
close_reason: inkx fix 9d122e9: calcItemOverflow with actual indicator overhead per-edge. User confirmed fixed.

title: TUI: 'j' from Kaiser Health in @next.md#inbox jumps cursor to board title
description: Navigating down ('j') in @next.md#inbox from the 'Kaiser Health' card causes the cursor to jump to the board title instead of the next card. Possible regression from km-tui.virtual-nav fix (40f8a894) or uncovered variant of km-tui-cursor-jump.
notes:
Investigation (2026-02-15): Extensive code analysis and testing. Could NOT reproduce the bug.

## What was tested
1. **Unit test on view-navigation**: `navigate("down")` from a link-type embed (Kaiser Health equivalent) correctly returns the next sibling card ID
2. **nodeIndex verification**: link-type embed nodes correctly appear in buildNodeIndex() with proper cardIndex
3. **Full rendering pipeline (68 cards)**: j navigates through all 68 mixed p/link embed cards without jumping to board
4. **Focused test (position 9)**: j from link-type embed at position 9 goes to next card correctly
5. **Real vault /tmp/vt**: Both navigate-down and full rendering pipeline work correctly with real data

## Code path traced
- handleCursorMove → handleVerticalNav → viewNavigation.navigate("down") → getSibling()
- getSibling uses repo.getChildren(parent_id) + indexOfChild for O(1) sibling lookup
- SELECT fast path uses nodeIndex.get(nodeId) — if not found, falls to selectionLevel="board" (the symptom)
- deriveColumnsFromRepo correctly includes type="link" nodes as body cards
- buildNodeIndex correctly maps all body cards including type="link"

## Hypothesis
The bug may be timing-related: if a file watcher mutation invalidates the repo snapshot between navigate() returning a valid target and the SELECT action looking it up in nodeIndex, the _layoutRepoVersion check in board-app-store.ts would trigger a full recompute with potentially stale columns. This is speculative — the static navigation logic is correct.

## Test file created
apps/km-tui/tests/inbox-cursor-jump.test.ts — 6 tests, all passing. Provides regression coverage for mixed p/link embed navigation in large columns.
close_reason: Cannot reproduce after extensive investigation by multiple agents across 2 sessions. 6 unit tests covering mixed p/link embed navigation all pass. 68-item TTY traversal smooth. title: Inline AST cleanup: eliminate stripForDisplay and stripFgColor holdovers
description:
## Goal
Complete the inline AST migration by eliminating remaining old-system holdovers.

## Tasks

### 1. Eliminate stripForDisplay() from views
`stripForDisplay()` (from @km/tree) pre-processes DB content before `<InlineText>`. The inline parser already handles block refs and fields, but:
- Fields render as styled `key:: value` instead of being stripped (card titles don't want this)
- Arrow refs `→ ^numericId` are partially handled (^id becomes blockref, but `→ ` stays)

**Fix**: The InlineRenderContext already has `stripRefs` — but we also need fields to render as empty in card title contexts. Either:
- Add field nodes to blockref-like "render empty" behavior when a context flag is set
- Or have stripForDisplay's work absorbed into the parser's km-syntax handling

Sites: TreeNode.tsx (2), NodeView.tsx (4), render.ts (1)

### 2. Eliminate stripFgColor() from views  
`stripFgColor()` strips ANSI fg colors from `infoSuffix` and `dateBadge` — pre-formatted ANSI badge strings.

**Fix**: Convert badge rendering from ANSI string construction to React components. Then selection highlighting works via `noColor` context or parent `<Text color={...}>` inheritance.

Sites: TreeNode.tsx (2), NodeView.tsx (2)

### 3. Clean up rich.ts
After #1 and #2:
- `stripFgColor` may become unused → delete
- `displayLength` is a thin wrapper around `string-width` → evaluate if still needed or consolidate
- If rich.ts becomes empty, delete it and update index.ts

### 4. Asana re-fetch (manual step, not code)
Cached JSON still has old Turndown output. Re-fetch to get clean HTML→mdast conversions:
```
bun km import asana --workspace Stabell --fetch --fetch-restart
bun km import asana --workspace Stabell --import --force
```
close_reason: Complete. All old-system holdovers removed: stripFgColor deleted from rich.ts, stripForDisplay eliminated from all views (replaced by hideFields context flag + arrow-ref parser pattern), ANSI badge builders converted to React components (DateBadge, InfoSuffix, BoardPillsView). Tests updated: strip-fg-color.test.ts deleted (covered by noColor props), infoSuffix prop test removed from node-view.test.tsx (prop removed). All 178 inline/node-view tests pass.

title: Leverage full Kitty + mouse input in km TUI
description:
With inkx now supporting full Kitty protocol and SGR mouse, wire these into km TUI for a dramatically better input experience.

## Keyboard (Kitty protocol)

- **Cmd+hjkl** for node shifting — DONE (km-infra.kitty-proto), works on Ghostty
- **Cmd+Z/Cmd+Shift+Z** — native undo/redo (currently Alt+u/Alt+r workaround)
- **Cmd+S** — save/sync (currently no shortcut)
- **Cmd+F** — search/filter (currently /)
- **Cmd+Enter** — create sibling, **Cmd+Shift+Enter** — create child
- **Key repeat events** — smooth continuous scroll when holding j/k (currently discrete)
- **Key release events** — hold Space to peek detail pane, release to dismiss
- **Option aliases** — keybindings accept opt/cmd as aliases for meta/super
- **Auto-detection** — Kitty protocol enabled automatically, graceful fallback on legacy terminals

## Mouse

- **Click** on card/node → select (move cursor to that item)
- **Click** on fold toggle (▸/▾) → expand/collapse
- **Click** on column header → focus column
- **Ctrl+Click** → multi-select nodes
- **Cmd+Click** on URL → open in browser
- **Scroll wheel** in columns → scroll the column
- **Scroll wheel** in detail pane → scroll detail content
- **Drag** (future) → reorder nodes

## Hit Registry Integration

Wire the existing HitRegistry into km TUI components:
- TreeNode registers click regions for each node
- CardColumn registers scroll areas and headers
- DetailPane registers its scroll area
- Dialog/modal components register at higher z-index

## Implementation Notes

Depends on inkx Kitty + mouse runtime wiring being complete (km-inkx.kitty-auto, km-inkx.mouse-runtime).
The command system already supports super modifier — this is about wiring mouse events and adding new Cmd+ shortcuts.
close_reason: Implemented: (1) kitty: true + mouse: true in runBoard() for auto-detection. (2) Cmd keybindings: ⌘Z/⌘⇧Z undo/redo, ⌘F search, ⌘Enter sibling, ⌘⇧Enter new item, ⌘C/X/V clipboard. (3) Mouse scroll wheel maps to cursor_up/down. (4) Left-click handler placeholder ready for HitRegistry. 341 command tests + 1751 TUI tests pass (6 pre-existing failures unrelated).

title: Global input mode state machine with push/pop context stack
description: O3 recommendation: Implement a global keyboard mode manager using a context stack pattern. States: 'command', 'insert', 'dialog:search', 'dialog:rename', etc. Push/pop model — opening any dialog pushes its mode, closing pops back to previous. Single source of truth for 'who handles keystrokes right now'. title: Level 1: Board useInput → useInputLayer migration
description:
Migrate Board.tsx from direct useInput to useInputLayer("board") as the base input layer.

## Current State
- Board.tsx line 872 uses `useInput()` directly for ALL key handling
- Dialogs (SearchDialog, ProjectPicker, NewItemDialog) already use `useInputLayer()`
- InputLayerProvider wraps BoardApp in tui.tsx line 192

## Problem
Board's `useInput` fires independently of the InputLayerProvider stack. When a dialog is open, BOTH the dialog's useInputLayer handler AND Board's useInput fire, causing potential double-handling.

## Target
- Board uses `useInputLayer("board", handler)` as the base layer
- Handler returns `true` to consume (always — Board is the bottom layer)
- Dialogs consume keys before Board via stack ordering
- Single unified input path through InputLayerProvider

- `apps/km-tui/src/views/board-input.ts` — handler returns boolean (consumed?)

title: Level 3: Centralize key handling in createApp() term:key handler
description:
Move ALL key handling from useInputLayer to createApp() centralized term:key handler.

## Current State (after L2)
- Board state in Zustand store via createApp()
- Keys still flow through useInputLayer → command bridge → command system
- InputLayerProvider still manages input dispatch

## Target
- createApp() term:key handler receives ALL keys before React
- Handler calls processKeyWithContext → command system → when predicates → action
- Actions update Zustand store via set()
- React re-renders via useApp(selector) subscriptions
- No useInputLayer, no InputLayerProvider needed

## Key Flow
```
stdin → TermProvider → term:key event → createApp handler
  → processKeyWithContext → @km/commands (when predicates)
  → action → set() Zustand store
  → React re-renders via useApp(selector)
```

## Dialog Input
Dialogs (search, new item, project picker) handled via when predicates:
- `when: textInputFocused` routes to TextEditTarget
- `when: isInlineEditing` routes to inline edit
- Dialog-specific keys (Escape, Enter) use dialog-specific predicates
- No per-dialog useInputLayer handlers needed

## Advantages
- Keys handled before React render cycle
- Single entry point for all input
- No race conditions from async useEffect registration
- Testable: driver.press() → term:key → same path as live app
- AI introspection: app.getState() gives full picture

## Files to Modify
- `apps/km-tui/src/board-app.ts` — add term:key handler
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/Board.tsx` — remove useInputLayer
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/SearchDialog.tsx` — remove useInputLayer, rely on when predicates
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/ProjectPicker.tsx` — same
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/NewItemDialog.tsx` — same
- `apps/km-tui/src/tui.tsx` — remove InputLayerProvider wrapper

## Dependencies
- Requires L2 (createApp + Zustand store) first

title: Remove manual dimension calculations — use inkx/flexx layout
description:
## Goal
Remove manual dimension calculations across km-tui in favor of automatic inkx/flexx layout. When inkx/flexx lacks needed features, fix them directly.

## Anti-Patterns to Eliminate

### A: Manual inner width/height calculation
```tsx
// BAD: manually subtracting border/padding
const innerWidth = Math.max(10, width - 6)
<Box width={innerWidth}>...</Box>

// GOOD: let flex layout handle it
<Box>...</Box>  // children auto-fill parent content area
```

### B: Manual text truncation
```tsx
// BAD: .slice() for truncation
const text = content.slice(0, width - 3)

// GOOD: inkx wrap=truncate
<Text wrap="truncate">{content}</Text>
```

### C: Manual centering with padding
```tsx
// BAD: compute padding to center text
const leftPad = Math.floor((width - text.length) / 2)
{' '.repeat(leftPad)}{text}{' '.repeat(rightPad)}

// GOOD: flex centering
<Box justifyContent="center"><Text>{text}</Text></Box>
```

### D: Manual separator/border drawing
```tsx
// BAD: repeat chars for HR
{'─'.repeat(innerWidth - 2)}

// GOOD: Box with borderBottom or dedicated <HR/> component
<Box borderBottom="single" />
```

### E: Manual Math.max guards
```tsx
// BAD: defensive guard against negative
Math.max(0, width - 2)
Math.max(10, width - 6)

// GOOD: inkx handles small/zero dimensions
<Box overflow="hidden">...</Box>
```

### F: width={N} on children inside flex parents
```tsx
// BAD: explicit width on flex children
<Box width={width}><Box width={innerWidth}>...</Box></Box>

// GOOD: flexGrow or omit width
<Box width={width}><Box flexGrow={1}>...</Box></Box>
```

### G: Manual height reserves for fixed elements
```tsx
// BAD: subtract header/footer heights
height={height - 3}

// GOOD: use flexGrow on the flexible area
<Box flexDirection="column" height={height}>
  <Box height={1} flexShrink={0}>header</Box>
  <Box flexGrow={1}>content</Box>
  <Box height={1} flexShrink={0}>footer</Box>
</Box>
```

### H: Manual column count calculation
```tsx
// MAY BE LEGITIMATE if inkx lacks auto-grid
Math.floor((width - 1) / (colWidth + 1))
// But check if inkx has flexWrap or similar
```

## Search Keywords
```
width - [0-9]   height - [0-9]   innerWidth   innerHeight
Math.max(       Math.min(        Math.floor(  Math.ceil(
.repeat(        .slice(0,        .padEnd(     .padStart(
width={         height={         width=\`
```

## Files with Manual Calcs
DetailPane.tsx, CardColumn.tsx, Board.tsx, ColumnsView.tsx, ListView.tsx, TabsView.tsx, HelpOverlay.tsx, FilterDialog.tsx, ConsoleModal.tsx, OverflowIndicator.tsx, render.ts, layout/path.ts
notes:
Audit found manual calcs in: DetailPane.tsx (innerWidth, separator repeat, maxEntries), CardColumn.tsx (width-1, width-2, height-2, separator repeat), ColumnsView.tsx (height-2, height-1), ListView.tsx (height-1), TabsView.tsx (height-3), HelpOverlay.tsx (centering math), FilterDialog.tsx (innerWidth), ConsoleModal.tsx (height calc), OverflowIndicator.tsx (manual centering), Board.tsx (colCount, cardsPerCol), render.ts (slice for truncation, colWidth), layout/path.ts (truncation). Categories: (A) Flex replacements: innerWidth, width-N on children. (B) Separator/border: repeat() for HR lines. (C) Text centering: manual padding. (D) Text truncation: .slice() instead of wrap=truncate. (E) Legitimate layout math: column counting, virtualization heights.
Also update .claude/skills/code/clean.md with Layout Anti-Patterns section when implementing.

title: Markdown prefix conversion: type '- ', '# ', '1. ', '[] ' to convert node type; backspace to strip
description:
Roam/Notion-style markdown prefix conversion during inline editing. Two behaviors:

## 1. Prefix Conversion (typing)

When the user types a recognized markdown prefix at the START of a node's content in edit mode, convert the node type and strip the prefix from content:

| Prefix typed | Resulting type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `- ` | li (bulleted) | Unordered list item, marker='-' |
| `* ` | li (bulleted) | Unordered list item, marker='*' |
| `1. ` | li (numbered) | Ordered list item |
| `# ` | oi (section) | h1 depth heading/section |
| `## ` | oi (section) | h2 depth |
| `### ` | oi (section) | h3 depth |
| `[] ` or `[ ] ` | task trait | Add task_marker '[ ]', keep type |
| `[x] ` | task trait | Add task_marker '[x]' (done) |
| `> ` | quote | Block quote |
| `--- ` or `*** ` or `___ ` | hr | Horizontal rule (integrates with km-tui.hr-edit) |
| `\`\`\` ` | code | Code block (fenced) |

Detection: trigger when user types the space (or newline for code fence) after the prefix. Strip the prefix from displayed content.

### HR Integration

The `---` prefix conversion integrates with km-tui.hr-edit: typing '---' + space converts the node to type=hr with content='---'. The HR edit spec handles subsequent editing, display (centered), and type reversion (backspace strips hr back to p).

## 2. Backspace Stripping (at beginning of line)

When user presses backspace at position 0 (beginning of content), strip features in priority order BEFORE merging with previous node:

1. **First**: If node has task trait → remove task_marker (keep type)
2. **Then**: If node type is non-paragraph (li, h, hr, quote, code, etc.) → convert to p
3. **Finally**: If already a plain p with no traits → merge with previous node (existing behavior)

This creates a progressive 'undo' of the node's special formatting before destructive merge.

## Node Types Reference (km-core)

Block types: p, h, code, quote, table, hr, html, math
Item types: oi (outline item), li (list item)
Link type: link

Not all types make sense for prefix conversion (table, html, math are complex structures). The prefixes above cover the common markdown shortcuts.

## Reference

Inspired by Decker's block editing model and Roam/Notion's markdown shortcuts.

1. Prefix auto-convert in TEXT_INSERT: typing markdown prefixes (- , * , + , 1. , # , ## , [] , [ ] , [x] , [/] , [!] , [-] , > ) at position 0 converts node type + strips prefix from edit field.
2. Backspace degradation in TEXT_DELETE_BACKWARD at cursor=0: strip task trait → convert non-p to p → merge with previous. Progressive degradation chain.
3. replaceContent() added to BlockEditTarget for inline content replacement during prefix conversion.
4. detectPrefixConversion() and backspaceDegradation() pure functions in block-ops.ts.
5. 27 new tests (20 prefix detection + 7 backspace degradation).
All 204 tree tests pass.

title: TUI architecture refactor: unified state, sync layout, fine-grained updates
description:
# Architecture Refactor: Cursor Movement < 5ms

## Goal
Cursor movement (j/k/h/l) must feel instant on a 1440-node board. Target: <5ms per keypress.

## Benchmark (2026-02-08, 1440 nodes, 200x60)
| Action | before | after phase 1 |
|--------|--------|---------------|
| cards j | 86ms | 73ms |
| list j | 46ms | 33ms |
| columns j | 40ms | 25ms |
| h/l | 93ms | 73ms |

## Phase 1 — COMPLETED
TreeRenderContext, flat Zustand store, reduced subscriptions. Commits: f8d46c51, 7463ae9c, e556e2da, ffebb213.

## Phase 2 — New architecture

### Primitives

**Per-node children cache** in repo. Lazy (populated on demand), surgical invalidation (addNode→bust parent, moveNode→bust old+new, updateNode→nothing, deleteNode→bust parent). All consumers benefit: rendering, navigation, path derivation.

**Path** (number[]). SlateJS-aligned structural coordinate system. Derived lazily from cursorNodeId via cache lookups (no SQL). Pure arithmetic helpers: parent, next, previous, compare, isAncestor.

**ViewNavigation**. One rule: move to the next selectable node in that direction. Cards are the only wrapping container — h/l from inside a card hits the card boundary. All cross-group lateral movement uses curswantY.

### Store (minimal)
```
cursorNodeId: string
rootId: string | null
foldedNodes: Set<string>
selectedNodes: Set<string>
viewMode: ViewMode
```

### Key input flow
```
keypress
  → view.navigate(dir, cursorNodeId, curswantY)
    → uses repo.getChildren (cached) to find next selectable node
  → store.set({ cursorNodeId: newId })
```

### Render flow
```
cursorNodeId changed → Zustand notifies
  → Board re-renders
    → useChildren(repo, rootId) — from cache
    → each Column: useChildren(repo, colId) — from cache
    → each Card: useChildren(repo, cardId) — from cache
    → isSelected via store selector (per component)
    → React.memo: only old + new cursor nodes re-render
  → inkx render pipeline
```

### Mutation flow
```
action → repo.mutate(...)
  → cache: surgical invalidation (affected parents only)
  → store.set({ cursorNodeId: targetId })
  → Zustand notifies → re-render
    → useChildren: cache miss for affected parents only, hits for rest
```

### What gets removed
ColumnsLayout, ColumnState, CardState, colIndex, cardIndex, subPath, subIndex, selectionLevel, isAtCardLevel, isInOutlineMode, COLUMN_HEADER_INDEX, recomputeLayout, deriveCursorPosition, deriveColumnsFromRepo, useColumns, useCursorPosition, updateLayout effect, store→React→store feedback loop, status bar position display, columnIndex/siblingIndex in command context.

### Implementation steps
1. Per-node children cache in repo
2. NodePath module (pathOf, nodeAt, siblings)
3. useChildren(repo, parentId) hook
4. ViewNavigation per view
5. Remove old layout system
6. Profile render pipeline
7. Targeted per-node signals if profiling shows selector cost matters

### Acceptance criteria
1. j/k/h/l < 5ms on 1440-node board, zoom < 20ms
2. No pre-computed layout indices — all derived lazily via Path + cache
3. No store→React→store feedback loop
4. One navigation rule, view-resolved
5. Documented in docs/design/visual-navigation.md
notes:
## Phase 3 Results (2026-02-08)
- cards_j: 76ms → 19ms (bench), ~13ms (isolated)
- content phase: 12ms → 3.4ms (scroll container optimization)
- layout phase: 3.4ms (top bar text changes → full Flexx recalc)
- VirtualList: no re-render when cursor within visible window
- Remaining bottleneck: layout recalculation on every j/k (top bar path text)
- h/l: 64ms (column change still expensive — full board re-render)
- zoom: 101ms (full re-layout expected)
close_reason: All 6 phases complete. cards_j: 76ms → 24ms (3.1x). Phase 1: nodeIndex O(1) lookup. Phase 2: CursorStore + silent mutation. Phase 3: Card self-subscription. Phase 4: VirtualList windowCalc scroll optimization. Phase 5: Node-based SelectionKey. Phase 6: Dead code cleanup.

title: Prevent Column re-render on within-column cursor movement
description:
# Prevent Column re-render on within-column cursor movement

## Problem
When j/k moves cursor between cards within the same column, Column re-renders because
`useIsCursorInColumn(colIndex)` returns a new object whenever `cardIndex` changes.
This cascades: Column → VirtualList → ~50 renderItem calls → ~50 Card memo comparisons.

Only 2 Cards actually differ (old/new cursor), costing ~3ms. The other ~20ms is wasted
on Column + VirtualList re-renders.

## Current: 24ms for j/k
- Column re-render (~8-12ms): useIsCursorInColumn returns new object
- VirtualList renderItem loop (~8-10ms): 50 renderItem calls
- 2 Card re-renders (~2-3ms): actual work
- Ink toTerminal (~2-3ms): buffer diff

## Target: <5ms for j/k (common case)

## Solution
1. Split `useIsCursorInColumn` into:
   - `useIsColumnSelected(colIndex)` → { isSelected, selectionLevel } — stable on j/k
   - `useCursorCardIndex(colIndex)` → number — for scroll tracking only

2. Column subscribes to `useIsColumnSelected` only — doesn't re-render on j/k

3. Add `ColumnScrollTracker` (null-rendering component) that:
   - Subscribes to `useCursorCardIndex`
   - Calls `virtualListRef.scrollToItem()` imperatively
   - Only causes VirtualList re-render when scroll offset actually changes

4. Card uses `useIsCursorAtCard` exclusively (remove prop dependency)

## Expected: Common case (cursor in window) = ~3ms
- Column: no re-render ✓
- VirtualList: no re-render (scroll offset unchanged) ✓
- 2 Cards: re-render via CursorStore (~3ms) ✓
notes:
## Progress (2026-02-08)
- Implemented Card CursorStore self-subscription (useIsCursorAtCard)
- Added useIsColumnSelected (stable on j/k), useCursorCardIndex (scroll tracking)
- Column still re-renders on j/k for VirtualList scrollTo prop
- Benchmark: 76ms → 40ms (cards_j avg)
- Imperative scroll approach gave 24ms but broke tests (act() flushing issue)
- Deep research request sent for 2nd opinion on achieving <5ms
close_reason: Column skip re-render achieved. Content phase 12ms→3.4ms. Total cards_j 76ms→~13ms across 3 sessions: CursorStore (76→24), Column skip + content optimization (24→13).

title: Performance regression after Phase 6 store refactor + NodeLine unification
description:
## Performance Regression After Phase 6 Store Refactor

The TUI is noticeably slower after the Phase 6 store refactor (commits b4d68773..e41bab6b).
This replaced RTK/immer/reselect with a plain Zustand-like store + useSyncExternalStore.

## Root Causes (ranked by impact)

### P0 — useApp() hook missing equality check (SMOKING GUN)

The `useApp()` hook in `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/runtime/create-app.tsx:214` does NOT compare
old vs new selected values before calling setState:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  return store.subscribe((newState) => {
    setState(() => selectorRef.current(newState))  // ALWAYS fires — no Object.is check
  })
}, [store])
```

Compare with zustand's `useStore`:
```tsx
// zustand checks: if (Object.is(currentSlice, nextSlice)) return;
```

Board.tsx now has 7 separate useAppStore() calls (lines 521-537):
- s.ui, s.boardState, s.toastQueue, s.layoutRegistry, s.setUI, s.dispatchBoard, s.updateLayout

Every store mutation fires ALL 7 subscriptions, each calling setState unconditionally.
React batches within a single event but the diffing/reconciliation cost is multiplied.

With RTK/reselect, memoized selectors would return the same reference for unchanged slices.
Now, every store change = 7 setState calls = 7 potential re-renders of Board.

### P0 — updateLayout() write-back creates render loop

Board.tsx:631-644:
```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  updateLayout(columnsLayout, selectedNode, derivedSelectionLevel, tuiBoardState)
}, [columnsLayout, selectedNode, derivedSelectionLevel, tuiBoardState, updateLayout])
```

This writes derived state BACK into the store after every render.
updateLayout calls set({layout, selectedNode, selectionLevel, tuiBoardState}),
which fires all subscribers again, potentially causing a second render cycle per keypress.

### P1 — assembleBoardState() creates new objects on every dispatch

board-app-store.ts:115-143: Every dispatchBoard call goes through withBoardState(),
which spreads `{...state, ...flatUpdate}` then calls assembleBoardState(),
creating a brand new boardState object even when only unrelated fields changed.
Board reads `s.boardState` — always gets a new ref → always re-renders.

### P1 — tuiBoardState useMemo has unstable deps

Board.tsx:609-623: `tuiBoardState` depends on `[boardState, columnsLayout]`.
Since boardState is a new object every dispatch (P1 above), this useMemo
NEVER memoizes — it recomputes every render, creating a new TUIBoardState.
This cascades through the entire component tree.

### P1 — N×useAppStore subscriptions in TreeNode

TreeNode.tsx:170-172: Every TreeNode instance subscribes to the store:
```tsx
const isFolded = useAppStore<BoardAppStore, boolean>(s => s.foldedNodes.has(node.id))
```

For a board with 200 cards, that's 200+ store subscriptions, each running their
selector on every store change. Without equality checks in useApp(), each fires setState.

### P2 — useBoardDialogs returns new handler object every render

use-board-dialogs.ts: Returns a plain object `{handleProjectSelect, handleProjectCancel, ...}`.
The individual handlers use useCallback, but the containing object is new every render.
BoardCore receives this as `dialogHandlers` prop — new ref every time.

### P2 — NodeLine renders renderRich() inline without memoization

shared-components.tsx:441: `{renderRich(title)}` is called on every render.
renderRich parses markdown + applies styles — non-trivial for 200+ visible nodes.
No React.memo on NodeLine means parent re-renders cascade.

### P3 — countVisibleDescendants is O(n) recursive and unused?

Board.tsx:785-807: This function exists but may not be called in the hot path.
If called during render, it walks the tree recursively for each visible card.

### P3 — new Set<string>() in tuiBoardState factory

Board.tsx:614: `selectedCards: new Set<string>()` creates a new Set every render.
While cheap, it means shallow comparison always fails for this field.

## Fix Plan (priority order)

1. **Fix useApp() equality check** — Add Object.is comparison in the subscriber:
   ```tsx
   store.subscribe((newState) => {
     const next = selectorRef.current(newState)
     setState(prev => Object.is(prev, next) ? prev : next)
   })
   ```

2. **Stabilize boardState ref** — Only create new boardState when flat fields actually change.
   Compare before/after in withBoardState.

3. **Remove or debounce updateLayout write-back** — Use a ref instead of store for layout,
   or gate the write with shallow equality check.

4. **Memoize useBoardDialogs return** — Wrap in useMemo.

5. **Add React.memo to NodeLine** — Trivial win for list rendering.

6. **Consider single useAppStore call** — Read all needed values in one selector to reduce
   subscription count from 7 to 1.
notes: 2026-02-07: Additional fix — updateLayout now uses silent mutation (bypasses Zustand set()) to eliminate double doRender() per keypress. Also added hit-count bell rate limiting for boundary auto-repeat (bellHitCount ≤ 2 fires, 3+ suppressed). Commit 37124478.
close_reason: Fixed: all P0-P1 items from analysis — useApp equality, updateLayout loop, assembleBoardState stability, tuiBoardState deps, bellState guard, Zustand no-ops.

title: H/L progressive fold/unfold — reveal more depth levels
description: H/L fold/unfold is currently binary (folded or not). User expects progressive behavior: pressing L multiple times reveals deeper levels of the tree (grandchildren, great-grandchildren), pressing H multiple times collapses deeper levels first. Current impl: FOLD_NODE adds card.id to foldedNodes set, UNFOLD_NODE removes it. No per-card depth tracking. Need: per-card outline depth that L increments and H decrements.
notes:
CORRECTION: Decker fold depth is CALCULATED, not stored.

Decker model:
- Each node has a boolean 'folded' property (like km's foldedNodes set)
- getFoldLevel(ed, at) COMPUTES min/max/curr depth by scanning which nesting levels are folded
- foldTreeMore(): finds shallowest unfolded depth in subtree → folds all nodes at that depth
- unfoldTreeMore(): finds deepest folded depth in subtree → unfolds all nodes at that depth
- Net effect: progressive fold/unfold without storing any depth number

km approach should match:
- Keep foldedNodes: Set<string> as-is
- H (fold_node): scan children of cursor card, find deepest visible level, fold all nodes at that level
- L (unfold_node): scan children of cursor card, find shallowest folded level, unfold all nodes at that level
- Progressive behavior emerges from the scan, no new state needed
close_reason: Progressive fold/unfold implemented. H walks subtree, finds deepest unfolded foldable nodes, folds them all. L finds shallowest folded nodes, unfolds them all. Fold depth is computed from tree walk, not stored. Verified in live TTY.

title: PTY integration tests: close the headless-vs-production testing gap
description:
## Problem: Headless Tests Pass, Production Breaks

Across 12+ sessions (2026-02-06 through 2026-02-08), headless tests consistently passed while the real TUI had visible bugs (visual bell flashes, cursor freezing on auto-repeat). Root cause: headless tests bypass the real async event pipeline:
- Headless: `board.press("j")` → `parseKey()` → `handleKey()` → synchronous
- Production: stdin → TermProvider → splitRawInput → event queue → processEventBatch → render

The key differences:
1. **No event batching**: headless tests process one key at a time, production batches auto-repeat bursts
2. **No timing**: headless tests are instantaneous, production has real latency between events and renders
3. **No terminal rendering**: headless tests check DOM/virtual buffer, production goes through the full ansi-diff → stdout pipeline

## Current State (partially fixed)

Created `apps/km-tui/tests/pty-integration.slow.spec.ts` using `createTtyEngine` (Bun PTY + @xterm/headless). This runs the REAL app in a REAL terminal pipeline (same stdin→terminal flow as production). 7 tests at 400x150:
- Startup, single j, burst j×10, rapid individual presses, large burst j×30, arrow keys, mixed keys

Also have TTY MCP tools (`mcp__tty__start`, `mcp__tty__screenshot`, etc.) for interactive visual verification.

## What's Still Missing

1. **PTY tests are slow** (~20-30s each due to startup + settle waits). Need faster warm-start or session reuse.
2. **No visual regression testing**: PTY tests check text content but not pixel-level rendering. Can't detect:
   - White flash artifacts
   - Cursor position rendering bugs
   - Color/style regressions
3. **No auto-repeat simulation**: `engine.press("j")` sends one key event. Real auto-repeat sends keys at 30Hz with specific timing. Need `engine.repeatKey("j", { count: 20, rateHz: 30 })`.
4. **No screenshot comparison**: `mcp__tty__screenshot` captures what we'd see, but no automated comparison between expected and actual.
5. **CI integration**: PTY tests need `*.slow.spec.ts` pattern to separate from fast tests.

## Proposed Approach

1. Add `engine.repeatKey()` to `tty-engine` that simulates real auto-repeat timing
2. Add screenshot capture to PTY tests (use `bufferToHTML()` from engine)
3. Create visual regression baseline snapshots
4. Speed up PTY tests: keep engine running across tests, use fresh vault per test
5. Integrate into `bun run test:slow` CI step
close_reason: PTY tests improved: added repeatKey() to TtyEngine, session reuse via beforeAll/afterAll, HTML snapshot capture, navigation correctness tests. Committed in 79e5acb7 and 397cc41.

title: Investigate reactive state management for repo→UI data flow
description:
## Problem

`repo.version` (auto-incrementing counter on mutations) is used in `useMemo` deps to invalidate UI caches. Issues:

1. **Fragile accounting**: Every mutation method must remember `version++` — miss one and UI goes stale silently
2. **Dead read**: `useMemo` deps only checked on re-render — relies on co-occurring UI dispatch
3. **Full recompute**: Any mutation recomputes entire `useColumns` derivation (all columns + all cards)
4. **Getter/setter needed**: `versionHolder` pattern exists because mutation methods are created before `repo` object — structurally necessary, not accidental

## Current architecture

```
mutation → version++ → hope React re-renders → useMemo checks version → re-derive all columns
```

useColumns reads repo.getChildren(rootId) + getChildren(columnId) for each column. Pure derivation, but creates fresh objects every time (breaks React.memo referential equality).

## Analysis of approaches

### Quick fix: SQLite total_changes()
Replace manual `version++` with `db.prepare("SELECT total_changes()").pluck().get()`. SQLite maintains this counter automatically — eliminates accounting risk. Same dead-read limitation.

### useSyncExternalStore (medium)
Add subscribe/getSnapshot to Repo. afterMutation hook notifies subscribers → React re-renders automatically. Eliminates dead-read problem. Still recomputes everything.

### Normalized reactive store (full solution)
Maintain a normalized store (Map<id, Node> + Map<parentId, childId[]>) alongside SQLite. Components subscribe to their slice via selectors. Only affected components re-render. This is what Decker does with Slate between Yjs and React.

## Reference: How others solve this

### Slate (rich text editor)
- Editor is mutable singleton (like our repo)
- `onChange` callback registered via WeakMap, fires on every operation
- Callback increments version `v` in React context → subscribers re-render
- Hooks: `useSlate()` (all changes), `useSlateSelection()` (selection only) — granular subscriptions
- Source: https://github.com/ianstormtaylor/slate/blob/main/packages/slate-react/src/components/slate.tsx

### Decker (boardliner)
- Zustand for UI state (selectedIds, draggingIds, editMode)
- Content lives in Yjs+Slate, NOT in Zustand
- Slate-Yjs bindings make Slate reactive to Yjs changes
- Per-component subscriptions via Zustand selectors
- Source: ~/Code/DZ/decker/apps/webapp/packages/decker-boardliner/src/store/

### SQLite reactivity landscape
- **Level 1 — Table-level invalidation**: Track which tables a query touches, re-run on any change. Simple, fast enough. Used by vlcn.io, ElectricSQL, observable-sqlite.
- **Level 2 — Differential dataflow**: Incremental computation pipelines, only process deltas.
- **Level 3 — Inverted index**: Index queries instead of data, pinpoint invalidation.
- Bun doesn't expose SQLite update_hook yet (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/4175)
- Since we're the only writer/reader, we don't need SQLite hooks — our afterMutation hook already knows when writes happen.
- References:
  - https://vlcn.io/blog/the-march-to-reactivity
  - https://riffle.systems/essays/prelude/
  - https://github.com/jorroll/observable-sqlite

## Key insight

Inline editing (useLineEdit) is local state — keystrokes don't touch repo. Repo mutations only happen on discrete actions (toggle status, move, delete, confirm edit). So full recompute frequency = discrete action frequency, not keystroke frequency. This may be fine for current scale.

## Recommendation

Start with useSyncExternalStore + total_changes() (eliminates accounting + dead reads). If profiling shows full recompute is too slow, upgrade to normalized store with per-component selectors.
close_reason: Grooming: investigation complete — useSyncExternalStore pattern implemented (MEMORY.md confirms). Remaining normalized store idea is speculative.

title: Unified task/block/item rendering and styling pipeline
description:
Unified NodeView component replacing 4+ separate rendering paths.

## API
```tsx
NodeView({ node, style, isSelected, width, height })
```

### Styles (detail levels)
| Style | Where | Content |
|---|---|---|
| board | Column header | title + child count |
| column | Section header (§) | section name + count |
| tab | Tab bar | title pill |
| line | Subitem in card/detail | icon + title (1 line, truncated) |
| card | Board column | icon + title + badges + N subitems (as lines) + overflow |
| detail | Side pane | metadata table + body + children (as cards) + backlinks |

### Cross-cutting props
- `isSelected` — cursor highlight (inverse/bold/border)
- Status-based styling — isDone/isDropped dims entire subtree; isWip/isBlocked get accent colors

### Key principle
Children recurse one level down: detail→card→line. Same rich text pipeline, same icon/color logic, same badge formatting at every level.

### Current duplication to eliminate
- TreeNode.tsx (card rendering)
- TaskDetailPane (detail rendering)
- FolderDetailPane (folder detail)
- ColumnItems (children in detail pane)
- tree-node-helpers.ts (style computation)
- detail-pane-helpers.ts (formatting)
- shared-components.tsx (card wrapper)

### Benefits
- 1 component, 1 code path for all node display
- Detail pane automatically gets bullet formatting, status icons
- Cards and detail pane always visually consistent
- Easier to add new styles (e.g., timeline, calendar cell)

title: Search dialog has input delay - keypresses eaten before dialog opens
description:
## Problem
When pressing `/` to open search, there's a noticeable delay before the dialog appears. Any keystrokes typed during this delay are lost/eaten, forcing users to wait before they can start typing their search query.

## Expected Behavior
Search dialog should open instantly (or near-instantly) so users can immediately start typing their search query in a fluid motion: `/china<Enter>` should work without pause.

## Actual Behavior
- Press `/`
- Delay of ~200-500ms before dialog appears
- Keypresses during delay are lost
- User must wait, then retype

## Impact
Breaks the fast keyboard-driven workflow. Users expect `/search<Enter>` to be a single fluid gesture.

## Potential Causes
1. React render cycle delay
2. Heavy `rawQuery(SELECT * FROM nodes)` on dialog mount
3. `useMemo` computation for initial results
4. Multiple re-renders during dialog setup

## Investigation
- Check if query can be deferred until after first render
- Consider showing dialog skeleton immediately, populate results async
- Profile render time with React DevTools
close_reason: Fixed: SearchDialog now uses useEffect + startTransition to defer heavy node query. Input handler registers immediately, preventing keypresses from being eaten.
